CENTRAL PROJECTS COORDINATION UNIT (CPCU)
Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs

                                         The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

                   Request for Expressions of Interest for Consulting Service

Country: The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for NRA (150km) Rural and Urban Road under the Gambia Infrastructure Project.

Procurement Method: Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS)   

Reference No.   GM-CPCU - MOFEA-527997-CS-CQS

Background:

The government of the Republic of the Gambia, under the World Bank (WB) Infrastructure Project has received an IDA Grant in an indicative amount equivalent to US$52.56 million available through The Gambia’s national IDA. The bank intends to apply a portion of this grant to eligible payments under a consultancy contract for the provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for NRA (150km) Rural and Urban Roads Construction under the Gambia Infrastructure Project.

The consulting services include Consultancy Services for the Preparation of the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for NRA (150km) Rural and Urban Roads Construction under the Gambia Infrastructure Project.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be collected from the address below:

Ms. Ndey Anta Taal Project coordinator, Central Project Coordination Unit, Royal Insurance Building, OIC highway, Kotu Tel:7555502/3971756. Email:/msanyang@cpcumof.gm /gip.procurement@cpcumof.gm / rsey@cpcumof.gm/mbt.senghore@cpcumof.gm  

The Central Project Coordination Unit – Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.:

Key Experts and Required Qualifications

The consulting firm must demonstrate:

  • Proven Experience: At least 10 years of experience in preparing RAPs for large-scale linear infrastructure projects (roads, railways, transmission lines) in Africa, with a minimum of 3 successfully completed in The Gambia and World Bank-approved RAPs.
  • Local Expertise: Demonstrated experience working in The Gambia, with in-depth knowledge of customary land tenure systems, local governance structures (Alkalo, Seyfo), and national laws (LACA 1991) and the Land policy 2026-2035

Evidence of Attestations/References of successfully performing similar assignments in The Gambia must be provided.

The team should be composed of the profiles:

No.

Key Expert

Minimum Qualification & Experience

1

Team leader

Senior Resettlement Specialist (International or National)

Qualification and Skills

  • MSc in Social Sciences, Economics, or a related field, with at least 10 years of demonstrated experience leading the preparation of Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) for World Bank–funded projects, specifically in the road sector (including rural and urban road development, rehabilitation, and upgrading). Proven expertise in managing land acquisition, physical and economic displacement, and stakeholder engagement associated with linear infrastructure. Fluent in English.

 

Experience

  • Demonstrated experience in linear infrastructure projects, particularly road development (rural, urban, and highway corridors), with a strong understanding of the associated social risks and resettlement impacts, including right-of-way acquisition, displacement of roadside economic activities, disruption of access (temporary or permanent), and impacts on roadside vendors, informal settlers, transport operators, and vulnerable groups.
  • Familiarity with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), especially:
    • Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement (ESS5)
  • Demonstrated proficiency in using social data analysis tools (e.g., SPSS, STATA) and GIS applications to analyze household survey and census data, map road alignments, right-of-way boundaries, and affected assets, and support socio-economic assessments and resettlement planning for road infrastructure project

Land Valuation and Asset Assessment Expertise:

  • Strong understanding of land tenure systems, asset inventory, valuation methodologies, and compensation frameworks applicable to land acquisition and involuntary resettlement. Experience working with national land valuation experts, cadastral authorities, and land administration agencies to ensure that asset valuation is conducted in line with replacement cost principles and national legal requirements.

2

Socio-Economic specialist/expert in Socio-economic surveys, gender, social inclusion and public consultation  (National)

 

Qualifications and Skills

  • MSc in Social Sciences. 8+ years’ experience in socio-economic surveys, gender analysis, vulnerability assessment, and participatory consultation in The Gambia. Fluency in English.

Experience

  • At least 10 years of demonstrated experience in social safeguards, including social risk and impact assessments, public and stakeholder consultations for infrastructure projects, and the design and implementation of inclusive and participatory engagement processes.

Demonstrated experience in conducting gender-responsive social assessments, including engagement with vulnerable and traditionally marginalized groups, and at least 5 years of experience in GBV/SEA/SH prevention and response, applying survivor-centered approaches and referral Mechanism.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with fluency in at least two local languages (e.g., Mandinka, Fula, Wolof, or other widely spoken local languages in The Gambia) to effectively facilitate stakeholder engagement and community consultations.

 

  • Ability to work with little supervision

3

Expert in Geographical Information System (GIS)

  • With a postgraduate degree (Master level) with at least 4 years of professional experience in his area of expertise, good knowledge of GIS software, database management system (Access, Excel), modelling and knowledge in photointerpretation and remote sensing.

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September 2023 revised February 2025 seventh edition September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) set out in the Procurement Regulations.

No.

Key Expert

Minimum Qualification & Experience

Team Leader- Senior Environmental and Social specialist

Environmental specialist

  • Strong IT and data skills (qualitative/quantitative methods, data management), and excellent communication (writing, presentations, reporting).

  • Fluent in English with excellent written and spoken skills. Working knowledge in one or more local languages will be an advantage

  • Experience establishing and operating project grievance mechanisms (community and worker GRMs), and in designing culturally appropriate engagement strategies.  
  • Familiarity with the World Bank ESF and national social regulations and practices.
  • Working proficiency in at least one local language (e.g., Fula, Mandinka, Wolof) is required.

4

Occupational Health and Safety Specialist

  • Master’s degree (or equivalent) in occupational health and safety, industrial hygiene, public health, environmental engineering, civil engineering, or occupational medicine.

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Individual Consultant Services

Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Consultant

Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC)

The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP), through the Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC), invites qualified individual consultants to express their interest in providing consulting services for conducting Decentralized Wastewater Treatment for the benefit of the Ministry of Local Government.

Background

The Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC) is financed by the World Bank and implemented under the overall oversight of the Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP). The project aims to:

  1. Increase employment opportunities for selected groups in targeted areas; and
  2. Improve the operational capacity of selected government institutions.

Under Component 3, Capacity Building of Selected Government Institutions, the Ministry of Local Government (MoLG) is implementing a capacity-building programme aimed at strengthening its institutional and technical capacities and enhancing the delivery of sustainable and resilient local public services.

As part of this programme, the Ministry seeks to strengthen its technical guidance for sustainable wastewater management. Many Palestinian Local Government Units (LGUs) continue to face challenges in providing wastewater services due to limited financial and technical capacities, the high costs of centralized systems, and environmental, planning, and geographical constraints, particularly in rural and underserved areas.

To address these challenges, the Ministry intends to engage an Individual Consultant to develop a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions. The assignment will support the Ministry and LGUs in planning, selecting, and implementing sustainable wastewater treatment solutions that are technically feasible, environmentally sound, and aligned with national priorities.

Assignment Objective

The objective of this assignment is to support Ministry of Local Government (MoLG) in developing a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions and to strengthen the capacity of MoLG and LGUs in planning, selecting, and implementing sustainable wastewater management solutions.

The assignment includes assessing existing needs, identifying priority locations, evaluating appropriate technology options, and developing technical guidance to support informed decision-making and the selection of solutions that are technically feasible, environmentally and socially sound, responsive to local conditions, and aligned with national priorities.

Scope of the Assignment

Under the overall supervision of the Ministry of Local Government, the Consultant shall provide technical expertise to support the development of a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions for Palestinian Local Government Units.

The proposed solutions and technical guidance shall be aligned with the relevant strategies and requirements of MoLG and the Palestinian Water Authority (PWA), as well as the applicable national reform and development plans.

The Consultant shall also prepare operational guidance as part of the assignment.

3.1 Main Duties and Responsibilities

The Consultant shall be responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

  1. Review relevant legislation, policies, strategies, technical guidelines, and existing studies related to wastewater management and decentralized wastewater treatment systems.
  2. Develop practical and scalable criteria for selecting appropriate decentralized wastewater treatment solutions, in full coordination with MoLG and with due consideration to operation and maintenance requirements.
  3. Assess the current status of wastewater management and identify the main technical, institutional, environmental, financial, and operational challenges faced by Palestinian Local Government Units.
  4. Assess existing wastewater management needs and develop objective criteria for identifying priority locations suitable for decentralized wastewater treatment solutions.
  5. Identify and evaluate appropriate small-scale decentralized wastewater treatment technologies and models applicable to different local contexts, taking into consideration:
    • Technical feasibility.
    • Environmental and social mitigation measures.
    • Sustainability.
    • Operation and maintenance requirements.
    • Cost-effectiveness.
  6. Develop a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions to support LGUs in selecting and planning appropriate wastewater management solutions.
  7. Prepare preliminary conceptual designs for selected priority locations, as appropriate.
  8. Conduct meetings and consultations with MoLG and relevant stakeholders, including PWA and PEA, throughout the assignment.
  9. Prepare and submit all required reports and deliverables, including the Inception Report, Assessment Report, Draft Technical Guidance Manual, Final Report, and Presentation, while incorporating comments received from MoLG.
  10. Ensure effective coordination with all relevant stakeholders, including MoLG, PWA, and PEA.
  11. Perform any other related tasks requested by MoLG within the agreed scope of the assignment.

Key Deliverables

The Consultant shall submit the following deliverables:

No.

Deliverable

Description

1

Inception Report

A comprehensive report outlining the assignment methodology, detailed work plan, implementation schedule, and stakeholder engagement approach.

2

Assessment Report

A detailed report assessing the current status of wastewater management in Palestinian Local Government Units and identifying the main challenges, existing gaps, and priority locations suitable for decentralized wastewater treatment solutions.

3

Draft Technical Guidance Manual

A draft Technical Guidance Manual presenting appropriate decentralized wastewater treatment technologies, technical selection criteria, preliminary conceptual designs for selected priority locations, implementation guidance, and operation and maintenance considerations to support MoLG and LGUs in planning and implementing sustainable wastewater treatment solutions.

4

Final Report and Presentation

A final report incorporating the comments of the Ministry of Local Government. The report shall include the finalized Technical Guidance Manual, selection criteria, operational guidance contributing to the capacity building of MoLG engineering staff and LGU staff, recommendations for improving service delivery, preliminary conceptual and economic designs, implementation guidance, documentation of consultations with key stakeholders, and a presentation summarizing the key findings of the assignment.

All deliverables shall be submitted to and formally approved by the Ministry of Local Government.

Reporting and Coordination

The Consultant shall work under the overall supervision of the Ministry of Local Government and shall closely coordinate with the relevant departments and stakeholders throughout the assignment.

The Consultant shall report directly to the designated focal point within MoLG and shall submit all reports, deliverables, and other required outputs for review and approval in accordance with the agreed work plan and timeline.

The Consultant shall maintain regular communication with the Ministry, participate in coordination meetings as requested, present the key findings and recommendations, and address comments received from the Ministry to ensure that all deliverables meet the required quality standards and the objectives of the assignment.

Duration of Assignment

The duration of the assignment shall be six (6) months from the date of signature.

Estimated Level of Effort

The Consultant shall provide the level of effort required to satisfactorily complete all tasks and deliver all outputs specified in these Terms of Reference within the contract period.

The estimated level of effort is fifty (50) working days.

Duty Station

The Consultant will be based at the Ministry of Local Government Headquarters in Ramallah, Palestine.

The Consultant shall undertake five (5) field visits to selected Local Government Units and project sites, as required and in coordination with the Ministry, to effectively carry out the assignment.

Required Qualifications and Experience

The Consultant shall have the following qualifications and experience:

  • At least a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Engineering, Sanitary Engineering, or another closely related discipline. Higher academic qualifications in a relevant field will be considered an asset.
  • Relevant professional experience in wastewater management, wastewater treatment, sanitation, and related infrastructure projects, demonstrating suitability for the assignment.
  • Demonstrated technical experience in decentralized wastewater treatment systems, technical assessments, development of technical models, conceptual designs, or other related wastewater management assignments.
  • Experience working with public-sector institutions and/or donor-funded projects, preferably projects financed by international development partners.
  • Strong reporting, communication, coordination, and networking skills.

Selection Method and Evaluation Criteria

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and based on the qualifications and experience of the applicant.

The evaluation will be conducted out of a total score of 100 points as follows:

Points

Evaluation Criterion

10

At least a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Engineering, Sanitary Engineering, or another closely related discipline. Higher academic qualifications in a relevant field will be considered an asset.

40

Relevant professional experience in wastewater management, wastewater treatment, sanitation, and related infrastructure projects, demonstrating suitability and adequacy for the assignment.

25

Demonstrated technical experience in decentralized wastewater treatment systems, technical assessments, development of technical models, conceptual designs, or other related wastewater management assignments.

10

Experience working with public-sector institutions and/or donor-funded projects, preferably projects financed by international development partners.

15

Reporting, communication, coordination, and networking skills.

100

Total

 

Only candidates obtaining a minimum technical score of 70 points may be invited for an interview, if deemed necessary by the evaluation committee.

The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP) is seeking to recruit qualified Data Analysis and Reporting Officer under the Social Recovery & Job Creation Project (SRJC), financed by the World Bank for the benefit of The Ministry of Local Government.

The selected Data Analysis and Reporting Officer will be assigned to work at the Ministry of Local Government — to support the Ministry of Local Government in strengthening institutional reporting, improving data analysis, and enhancing the quality and consistency of information used for planning, monitoring, and decision-making.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Data Analysis and Reporting Officer will support the collection, validation, analysis, and reporting of institutional data and information. The Officer will coordinate with relevant departments to improve reporting processes, prepare analytical reports, and support evidence-based planning and institutional performance.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collect, organize, validate, and analyze reports and data received from relevant departments.
  • Prepare periodic reports, statistical summaries, analytical reports, briefing notes, and presentations.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments to ensure the timely submission and accuracy of reports and data.
  • Consolidate institutional reports and ensure the consistency and completeness of information.
  • Maintain and update reporting records, databases, and related documentation.
  • Develop dashboards, charts, and reporting tools to support management decision-making.
  • Review data quality and identify inconsistencies or gaps requiring follow-up.
  • Support the preparation of reports required by senior management, development partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Recommend improvements to reporting systems and data analysis practices.
  • Maintain organized electronic and hard-copy records related to reporting and data analysis.
  • Perform any other related duties as may be assigned by the Director General of the Projects Department.

Job Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Business Administration, Statistics, Information Systems, Management Information Systems, Economics, Public Administration, or any other related field.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in reporting, data analysis, institutional reporting, or administrative coordination.
  • Demonstrated experience in preparing reports, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, and presenting findings.
  • Experience working with government institutions or internationally financed projects is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience in Power BI, Excel dashboards, or other data visualization tools is considered an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and report-writing skills in both Arabic and English.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work effectively under pressure.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-7.4.1 – Project Manager 1)

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

Assignment Title: Project Manager 1

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.4.1

Ukraine and World bank have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of the Consultant's assignment is to ensure effective project management and coordination within the Cross-sectoral Project Management Unit of the NUS Implementation Office to achieve reform objectives.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 25, 2026.  

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Project Manager 1

Contract No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.4.1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

URTF Grant No. TF0C5794

 

 BACKGROUND

 

Ukraine and the World Bank have signed the agreements for the Program "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program" (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN). The objectives of the LEARN are: to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system.

 

The total financing for the Operation is US$451 million using a combination of the World Bank's financial instruments: Program-for-Results (PforR) complemented by Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 million credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 7626-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 9721-UA). Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

Furthermore, US$31.1 million in Additional Financing is provided through grant resources, consisting of US$30.0 million from the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund and US$1.1 million from the Global Partnership for Education Fund. This additional financing is formalized under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0D0612; GPE GRANT NUMBER TF0D0613), and supports activities related to the continued implementation of the Program.

 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan.

LEARN will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

The objectives of the Program are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The Program is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with the support of the World Bank Group. The implementation period is 2024-2027.

More detailed information is given at the link https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

 

The Operation will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

For this program, "teaching and learning conditions" refer to three critical factors of education service delivery:

i. safety, including shelters as a pre-condition for schools to open for in-person learning and free and inclusive school bus transportation for students living further distances from schools;

ii. learning materials, especially updated textbooks and age-appropriate learning materials in line with the NUS model; and

iii. teachers trained on NUS standards, principles, and the use of the updated learning materials.

Meanwhile, "management capacity of the education system" refers to institutional capabilities to plan, allocate, and monitor resources based on robust data at the student and school levels.

The NUS Implementation Office (NIO) will be established by the Ministry as an advisory and consultative body. The NIO's primary purpose is to support and implement the New Ukrainian School (NUS) reform by providing expert guidance, strategic oversight, and coordination of reform initiatives across Ukraine.

 OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to ensure effective project management and coordination within the Cross-sectoral Project Management Unit of the NUS Implementation Office to achieve reform objectives.

SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Manages specific projects and initiatives within the NUS reform implementation.
  • Ensures coordination between different units and teams to achieve project objectives.
  • Develops and implements project plans, including timelines, resources, and budgets.
  • Conducts monitoring and reporting on project progress.
  • Identifies and manages project risks, develops mitigation strategies.
  • Maintains communication with all project stakeholders.

 

REPORTING

Project Manager 1 reports directly to the Operational Deputy Head of New Ukrainian School Implementation Office. For operational matters, works in coordination with relevant unit heads.

Monthly reports must include details of progress, challenges, and tasks completed, along with time sheets.

PROVIDED RESOURCES

MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES shall provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • At least 2 years of professional experience in project management and administration/implementation
  • At least 1 year of experience in collaboration with national and local government authorities
  • At least 2 years of experience in education sector, preferably school education
  • Experience of collaboration with international financial or donor organizations
  • Advanced spoken and written English (upper intermediate or better level of English including knowledge of project management terminology)
  • Fluency in Ukrainian

Desired skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in managing educational projects
  • Strong understanding of project management methodologies
  • Knowledge of NUS reform principles and objectives
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills
  • Ability to work in conditions of high uncertainty
  • Crisis management experience

PERIOD AND LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until August 31, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES) during the Project financing period.

The Consultant shall provide his/her services on a full-time basis.

The incumbent will be based in Kyiv, Ukraine. The Consultant should be required and expected to take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua, Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua  indicating the email subject: " LEARN-IC-NIO-7.4.1: Selection of Project Manager 1: [NAME]".

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 25, 2026.

If the Consultant fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the Consultant's application.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.2-ECEIT-TA3 - Junior Project Manager for the Development of the Automated Information Complex for Education Management (AIKOM) for Preschool Education)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Junior Project Manager for the Development of the Automated Information Complex for Education Management (AIKOM) for Preschool Education

No. LEARN-2.2-ECEIT-TA3

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to support project management for the development of the AIKOM software and hardware module in the field of preschool education, including participation in work planning and coordination, monitoring of task implementation, support of communication with stakeholders, and administrative support for the processes of development and acceptance of functionality. 

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 25, 2026.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for the provision of consulting services (individual consultant)

Junior Project Manager for the Development of the Automated Information Complex for Education Management (AIKOM) for Preschool Education

 

Procurement No. LEARN-2.2-ECEIT-TA3
Program "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine" (LEARN)
Grant URTF No. TF0D0612

I. Background

The Government of Ukraine is implementing a comprehensive reform of the education sector aimed at strengthening teaching and learning conditions and enhancing management capacity at all levels of education, which is one of the key tasks on Ukraine's path to EU accession. With the adoption in 2024 of the new Law of Ukraine "On Preschool Education", which entered into force on 1 January 2025, active transformation processes have also encompassed the preschool education sector.

Early childhood and preschool education ranks first among the strategic priorities defined by the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 276 dated 7 March 2024. The ultimate goal of the reform is to ensure access to quality preschool education for every child, including children with special educational needs. This goal is to be achieved through a number of strategic objectives: accessibility, highly qualified and motivated staff, alignment of the quality and content of education with European requirements, and the functioning of effective systems for monitoring and quality assessment, management, and financing.

European Commission's 2024 Communication on EU Enlargement Policy notes the steps taken as a certain degree of progress. It highlights the following task — to ensure the implementation of preschool education legislation that introduces measures aligned with EU principles and focuses on quality early childhood education, guaranteeing access for children of early and preschool age, fair rules for the operation of preschool education entities, and decent working conditions for staff.

The implementation of this reform is also accompanied by the development of a draft Preschool Education Development Strategy, presented during the "First Steps Forward" event, new secondary legislation, and additional budget allocations.

These reforms, the most transformative in over three decades, will be implemented in two phases. The first phase envisages capacity development at the national and local levels for the implementation of reforms on a limited scale, in approximately 35 territorial communities, combined with careful process evaluation to prepare for scale-up. The second phase envisages the implementation of the Strategy at the national level.

To support the first phase of the preschool education reform, the Government has requested additional resources under the technical assistance component financed through the Investment Project Financing instrument of the "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine" (LEARN) project.

In 2024, Ukraine and the World Bank signed agreements for the "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine" (LEARN) operation.

The objective of LEARN is to: (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen the management capacity of the education system. Total financing for LEARN amounts to USD 451.0 million and combines the following World Bank financial instruments: Program-for-Results (PforR) financing – USD 389.9 million, and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – USD 61.1 million.

Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a loan of USD 235 million provided from Bank resources and supported by the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, financed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized through a Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No. 9721-UA). An additional USD 150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the IDA Crisis Response Window, as set out in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No. 7626-UA). On 1 July 2025, a Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No. 7905-UA) in the amount of USD 4.9 million.

In addition, USD 30 million of Investment Project Financing (IPF) is provided under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GRANT URTF No. TF0C5794). On 19 December 2025, a Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, jointly acting as the Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GRANT GPE No. TF0D0613, GRANT URTF No. TF0D0612), in the amount of USD 31.1 million.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine has established the Early Childhood Education Development Office (ECEDO). Functioning as a technical implementation office within the Ministry, ECEDO provides operational and expert support to coordinate overall reform efforts across several areas, including access and financing, education content and teacher professional development, inclusion, quality assurance, legal and regulatory frameworks, and cross-sectoral cooperation. The Office will also be responsible for monitoring the implementation of reforms in early childhood and preschool education (ECPE). The establishment of ECEDO strengthens the capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to manage donor-financed technical assistance, support participating communities, ensure coherence among reform components, and integrate project results into national systems for long-term sustainability and scalability.

To improve information support for management activities in Ukraine's education sector, the software and hardware complex "Automated Information Complex for Education Management" (AIKOM) was established, with its tasks, purpose, and operating procedures defined by Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 1255 of 2 December 2021. The tasks to be performed by the Consultant will contribute to strengthening management capacity in the field of preschool education by supporting the development of the relevant AIKOM module.

II. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of this assignment is to support project management for the development of the AIKOM software and hardware module in the field of preschool education, including participation in work planning and coordination, monitoring of task implementation, support of communication with stakeholders, and administrative support for the processes of development and acceptance of functionality.

III. Scope of Work

1. Task Planning and Coordination

  • maintain the up-to-date task plan and project schedule;
  • maintain the task backlog and participate in prioritization together with the Project Manager;
  • track task completion deadlines and record implementation status.

2. Team and Stakeholder Coordination

  • organize working meetings, take minutes, and record decisions made;
  • support communication between the development team and business stakeholders;
  • prepare informational materials for project stakeholders.

3. Documentation and Reporting

  • prepare status reports on project progress;
  • maintain the task, risk, and issue register (issue/risk log);
  • participate in the preparation of presentation and reporting materials for management and the donor.

4. Risk and Change Management

  • participate in identifying project risks and assessing their impact;
  • participate in supporting the change management process and prepare accompanying documentation.

5. Administrative Support of the Project

  • organize working meetings and workshops;
  • maintain project documentation in the task management system (ClickUp and others);
  • organize and archive project materials.

IV. Expected Deliverables

  • Updated task plan and project schedule.
  • Meeting minutes and register of decisions made.
  • Status reports on project progress.
  • Register of project tasks, risks, and issues.
  • Project documentation in the task management system.

V. Performance Indicators

The Consultant's performance will be assessed against the following indicators:

  • timeliness of completing assigned tasks and preparing materials;
  • quality of maintaining project documentation and reporting;
  • active participation in team processes and communication with stakeholders;
  • diligence in supporting deadline monitoring and risk management processes;
  • positive assessment by the Project Manager of the quality of support provided.

VI. Reporting and Coordination

The Consultant reports to the Project Manager for the development of the Automated Information Complex for Education Management (AIKOM) for preschool education and works under his/her direct supervision. The Consultant coordinates activities with the Team Leader of the World Bank's operations management team.

The Consultant submits monthly reports to the Project Coordinator or Co-coordinator of the project in hard copy. The reports must contain a description of the services provided by the Consultant during the reporting period.

VII. Duration and Format of the Assignment

The Consultant will provide services until 31 December 2028. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance of the assignment and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the MoES.

The Consultant will provide services under this Contract on a full-time basis for the entire duration of the contract, with a level of engagement equivalent to full-time employment, to the extent necessary for the proper performance of the tasks defined in the Scope of Work.

VIII. Minimum Qualification Requirements

  • higher education (not lower than a bachelor's degree) in information technology, project management, general management, or other relevant fields;
  • at least 1 year of experience in a position of Junior Project Manager, Project Assistant, Project Coordinator, or a similar role (experience in IT projects will be an advantage);
  • basic knowledge of project management methodologies and practices (Agile/Scrum, Kanban, Waterfall);
  • confident use of task management and document management tools (ClickUp, Jira, Trello, MS Office/Google Workspace);
  • ability to prepare meeting minutes, status reports, and project documentation;
  • attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and ability to work effectively in a team;
  • proficiency in Ukrainian at a level sufficient for business communication and documentation; English at a level not lower than B1.

IX. Desirable Skills and Qualifications

  • experience participating in projects in the public sector or within international technical assistance;
  • basic understanding of the education sector and/or digital government registry processes;
  • meeting facilitation skills;
  • practical experience participating in Agile/Scrum processes (sprints, daily stand-ups, retrospectives).

X. Application Package

Interested candidates should submit their CV in Ukrainian and English to: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua,

copy: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and marina.chubenko@mon.gov.ua .

Email subject line: "Selection for the position of Junior Project Manager, Preschool Education Module, AIKOM: [NAME]".

Application deadline: August 25, 14:00 Kyiv time.

If the applicant fails to submit a CV in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the applicant's submission.

Request for Expressions of Interest (REoI)

Country: Lebanon
Project: Green Agri-Food Transformation for Economic Recovery (GATE) Project
Implementing Agency: Kafalat SAL
Assignment Title: Credit Administration Officer - PMU (Sub-component 1.2)
Reference No.: LB-KAFALAT-564926-CS-INDV

1. Background

The Government of Lebanon has secured financing under the Green Agri-Food Transformation for Economic Recovery (GATE) Project, supported by the World Bank. Under this Project, Sub-component 1.2 (“Access to Finance for SMEs”) is implemented by Kafalat SAL as the designated Implementing Agency. This Sub-component supports the provision of direct SME lending managed and administered by Kafalat, with a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) responsible for credit operations, fiduciary oversight, procurement, safeguards, and monitoring. To ensure effective execution, Kafalat will establish this PMU in line with the Subsidiary Agreement and Project Operations Manual (POM).

2. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of this assignment is to recruit a full-time Credit Administration Officer to support the efficient administration and operational processing of SME lending activities under Subcomponent 1.2, ensuring completeness of documentation, compliance with internal procedures and project requirements, proper file management, timely coordination with stakeholders, and accurate updating of records and systems.

3. Scope of Work

The Credit Administration Officer will:

  • Receive, organize, and maintain SME loan applications and supporting documentation, ensuring proper filing, archiving, scanning, and maintenance of complete physical and electronic credit files.
  • Verify completeness and accuracy of all legal, financial, operational, and collateral-related documentation in accordance with the Lending Manual, application checklist, and operational procedures.
  • Ensure all required declarations, undertakings, approvals, and legal documents are properly signed and filed.
  • Track and monitor the validity and renewal of supporting documentation, including licenses, commercial registrations, insurance policies, and collateral-related records.
  • Support the preparation and circulation of loan files for appraisal and Credit Committee review.
  • Check that every SME credit file contains all mandatory legal documents required prior to loan approval and disbursement, in line with Kafalat's internal procedures and the GATE Project legal framework.
  • Coordinate with internal departments to ensure timely processing of applications and follow up with SMEs on missing documents, outstanding conditions, and other collateral-related matters.
  • Prepare and submit requests for credit information via the Central des Risques platform, and coordinate with Compliance, AML/KYC, and credit bureau agencies to ensure proper maintenance of customer due diligence documentation.
  • Maintain accurate, consistent, and up-to-date information within the Loan Management System (LMS) and other tracking systems, including updated records of all submitted, pending, approved, rejected, and disbursed applications.
  • Support the implementation and enhancement of credit administration processes, controls, and operational workflows, and escalate operational bottlenecks or file deficiencies to management.

A detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) is available upon request at: yolla@kafalat.com.lb.

4. Qualifications and Skills

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Banking, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, Law, or a related field. A Master's degree or professional certification is an asset.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in credit administration, loan operations, credit documentation, or banking operations, preferably within a commercial bank or financial institution.
  • Good working knowledge of Lebanese legal and regulatory requirements applicable to commercial documentation and collateral (pledges, mortgages, guarantees).
  • Strong knowledge of lending operations, collateral management, and credit administration procedures.
  • Experience working with Loan Management Systems (LMS), banking systems, or credit administration platforms.
  • Good understanding of KYC, AML, compliance, and documentation requirements.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Excellent command of Arabic and English; strong communication and coordination skills.

5. Application Process

Interested qualified candidates are invited to submit their Expressions of Interest (EOI), including:

  • A cover letter highlighting relevant experience.
  • An updated CV.
  • Contact details of at least two professional references.

Submissions must be sent by email to yolla@Kafalat.com.lb   with the subject line: “EOI - Credit Administration Officer “ no later than 26/08/2026.

6. Selection

A shortlist will be established based on qualifications and relevant experience. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

The Government of Indonesia
Global Environment Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project
Grant No.: TF B8114
Assignment Title: Urban Planning Specialist
(National Consultant)
Reference No.: ID-TRANSPORT - BAPPENAS-561667-CS-INDV

The Government of Indonesia, through the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas), has received grant funding from the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) through the World Bank. Part of this funding is allocated for individual consultant services.

The Individual Consultant – Urban Planning Specialist will be assigned to the Directorate of Connectivity and Logistic Infrastructure, Bappenas. The Consultant will work closely with the team of Individual Consultants to provide technical oversight, coordination, and documentation support for the supervision and quality assurance of the SUMP development in Balikpapan and Palembang, which is carried out by the contracted consulting firms.

The main tasks of the Individual Consultant include:

  1. Validation for the Functional Urban Areas (FUA) Delineation. Support the review of the Functional Urban Area (FUA) delineation proposed by the consulting firms for the Balikpapan and Palembang SUMP, ensuring consistency with prevailing statutory planning documents, including the RPJMN, RPJMD, RTRW, and RDTR, and with regional policy. Contribute literature reviews and case studies on FUA delineation in comparable Indonesian and international contexts to strengthen the review;
  2. Supervision to Spatial and Urban Planning Analysis. Assist in reviewing spatial and urban planning aspects of the SUMP, including land use integration, urban growth patterns, and accessibility considerations. Support the identification of relevant data needs and analysis of spatial information, and help ensure alignment between transport planning and urban development strategies in both cities;
  3. Supervision of Vision Alignment and System Diagnosis. Deliver rigorous technical supervision and validation on the consulting firms' outputs regarding vision alignment, baseline assessments, and environmental mobility analysis to ensure compliance with national strategic frameworks;
  4. Evaluation of Strategic Planning Development and Action Packages. Provide critical evaluation and quality assurance for the risk registers, KPI frameworks, institutional strengthening strategies, intervention scenario analyses, and the final design viability of the proposed action packages. Including technical support to the review and validation of frameworks related to transit-oriented development (TOD) and the integrated planning of strategic urban areas, ensuring that proposed directions are consistent with TOD principles, sustainable urban form, and the cities' broader spatial and economic development strategies;
  5. Technical Support for SUMP Supervision. Support the team of Individual Consultants in reviewing the consulting firms’ outputs, including methodologies, analytical approaches, and draft reports. Assist in compiling inputs, preparing review materials, and ensuring that comments and recommendations are properly documented and communicated to the consulting firms.

To support the main tasks, the Consultant may undertake the following supporting activities, but not limited to:

  1. Coordination and documentation support. Assist in coordinating meetings, FGDs, and consultations related to the urban planning dimensions of the SUMP. Track the progress of related activities and maintain records of communications, deliverables, and review documentation associated with the consulting firms’ work;
  2. Capacity building and technical guidance of the Directorate. Work alongside the team of Individual Consultants to deliver technical guidance and capacity improvement to the Directorate in key areas such as integrated transport planning through sustainable urban mobility plan principles, infrastructure investment planning, creative financing, Traffic Demand Management (TDM), and development of Integrated Transport Authority (ITA) frameworks.

The individual consultant services are expected to start in September 2026 and perform the service for 4 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found in the following link: https://link.bappenas.go.id/08192026035805

  • Essential Qualification
  1. Bachelor’s degree or higher in urban and regional planning, urban planning and real estate, urban development studies, civil engineering, transportation engineering, environmental engineering, environmental studies, or a relevant field. A master’s degree in a relevant field is an advantage;
  2. A minimum of work experience of 4 years in the urban planning, spatial planning, or urban development sector is required. Exposure to the transport or urban mobility sector is preferred;
  3. Familiarity with the Indonesian spatial and development planning system, including RTRW, RDTR, RPJMN, RPJMD, and related regulatory instruments;
  4. Proficient in performing quantitative and qualitative data analysis in transportation sector and demonstrating strong communication and writing skills in professional English (proven by policy papers/books/studies/journals/research/essay/report/ToR sample in English) and Bahasa Indonesia.

The Government of Indonesia, through the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas), has received grant funding from the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) through the World Bank. Part of this funding is allocated for individual consultant services.

The Individual Consultant – Transportation Specialist will be assigned to the Directorate of Connectivity and Logistics Infrastructure, Bappenas, and will work closely with the team of Individual Consultants in providing technical guidance and supervision for the development of the Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP) in Balikpapan and Palembang, which is carried out by the contracted consulting firms.

The main tasks of the Individual Consultant include:

  1. Task 1: Technical Oversight and Advisory of SUMP Development, Including Knowledge Integration and Cross-Cutting Inputs.
    1. Provide technical advisory support to the Balikpapan and Palembang SUMP development process by integrating relevant lessons learned from previous studies, national programs, and international best practices into the consulting firms' work.
    2. Provide technical review and supervision of the consulting firms' data collection activities, survey implementation, and analytical methodologies, including household surveys, O/D Matrix, four-step transport model, level of service (LOS), non-motorized transport (NMT), travel demand management (TDM), and other technical analyses to ensure methodological soundness and analytical consistency
    3. Provide strategic inputs on cross-cutting topics including, but not limited to, multimodal integration, feeder concepts (e.g., the Palembang LRT feeder network), angkot/BRT reform, non-motorized transport (NMT) and accessibility, transport demand management (TDM), and land use/transit-oriented development (TOD) integration. Recommendations shall support the consulting firms and the Directorate in strengthening the technical direction and strategic coherence of each city's SUMP as it develops.
  2. Task 2: SUMP Development Deliverables Oversight.
    1. Conduct oversight of the SUMP consulting firms' deliverables (step 1 until step 15) for Balikpapan and Palembang to ensure completeness and consistency against the required deliverable items set out in each firm's Term of Reference, including data collection and survey outputs, transport modelling methodology and outputs, existing conditions assessment, vision development, policy measures, investment prioritization, and implementation strategy.
    2. Maintain and update a consolidated deliverables checklist tracking the status of each required item (submitted / complete / pending / needs revision) for both cities, and provide written technical comments where gaps, delays, or inconsistencies are identified.

To support the main tasks, the Consultant may undertake the following supporting activities, but not limited to:

  1. Task 3: Advisory, Capacity Building and Coordination Support to the Directorate.
    1. Capacity building and technical guidance of the Directorate. Work alongside the team of Individual Consultants to deliver technical guidance and capacity improvement to the Directorate in key areas such as integrated transport planning through sustainable urban mobility plan principles, infrastructure investment planning, creative financing, Traffic Demand Management (TDM), and development of Integrated Transport Authority (ITA) frameworks.
    2. Coordination of GEF Indonesia SCIP Component 2 Activities. Support the coordination and monitoring of activities under GEF Indonesia SCIP Component 2 related to SUMP development, ensuring consistency between the outputs of the consulting firm and the overall program objectives.

The individual consultant services are expected to start in September 2026 and perform the service for 4 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found in the following link: https://link.bappenas.go.id/08192026034658

The Directorate of Connectivity and Logistics Infrastructure at the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency now invites eligible individual consultant (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are the relevant experience of the individual consultant in:

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Essential Qualification
  1. Minimum of a Master's degree in transportation system, transportation engineering, civil engineering with transport specialization, or a related field including urban planning, with at least 1 year of relevant work experience in urban transportation planning, transport modelling, or sustainable urban mobility; OR a Bachelor's degree in civil engineering or urban planning with at least 4 years of relevant work experience in urban transportation planning, transport modelling, or sustainable urban mobility;
  2. Demonstrated working experience in environmental and/or social safeguarding aspects of infrastructure or urban development projects (e.g., familiarity with donor safeguard frameworks such as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), AMDAL, or equivalent);
  3. Familiarity with the Indonesian urban transport planning context, including relevant national policies and regulations governing urban mobility and public transport;
  4. Proficient in performing quantitative and qualitative data analysis in transportation sector and demonstrating strong communication and writing skills in professional English (proven by policy papers/books/studies/journals/research/essay/report/ToR sample in English) and Bahasa Indonesia;
  • Additional Qualifications (an advantage)
  1. Has experience in a minimum of one (1) SUMP/Pre-FS/FS project (proven by CV and supporting document(s) such as contracts, acknowledgment letter, or other related documents);
  2. Demonstrated strong familiarity with Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP) development principles – including data collection and analysis, scenario development, and staged implementation;
  3. Demonstrated hands-on experience in at least three of the following: travel demand modeling (including four-step model application), travel survey design and analysis (household, roadside, on-board), public transport network planning and analysis, NMT planning, and travel demand management;
  4. Experience working on national/international development agency operations such as Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas)/Ministry of Transportation/World Bank/Asian Development Bank/USAID/GIZ/GCF/KIAT, etc.

The firm(s) shall demonstrate that their core business and principal areas of practice are in: (i) Transportation and highway engineering; (ii) Transport infrastructure planning and advisory; (iii) Engineering feasibility studies; and (iv) Public-Private Partnership (PPP) transaction advisory services; or closely related fields, for a period of at least fifteen (15) years.

b) Relevant experience 

The firm(s) shall demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity, undertaken within the last ten (10) years in a comparable operating environment. The assignments shall collectively demonstrate experience in the following areas: (i) Transport infrastructure feasibility studies; (ii) Highway planning and engineering design; (iii) Traffic engineering, transport demand forecasting and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS); (iii) Environment and Social safeguards studies for transport infrastructure projects; and (iv) PPP Advisory Services including project structuring, financial analysis, procurement support, and transaction management for the selection of private partners.

data.institution: Ministry of Economy and Planning
data.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

MINISTRY OF PLANNING

ACCELERATING ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION AND JOB CREATION PROJECT

Loan No.: IBRD-95270

Project ID: P178035

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND TECHNICAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL STUDIES, AND ENVIRONMENTAL LICENSING FOR LAST-MILE INFRASTRUCTURE IN HUAMBO, BIÉ AND BENGUELA

Reference No. 95CS2/MINPLAN/26

 

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the Development and Technical, Environmental, Social Studies, and Environmental Licensing for Last-Mile Infrastructure in Huambo, Bié and Benguela.

Consulting Services (“the Services”) aim to provide technical support to the Ministry of Planning, through the DIVERSIFICA+ Project Implementation Unit (PIU), in all phases prior to the execution of last-mile infrastructure projects in the provinces of Huambo, Bié, and Benguela. The role of the consulting firm includes:

  1. Identifying the technical, economic, and social needs of the selected productive infrastructures, mapping existing site conditions, and inventorying current infrastructure assets in the intervention areas;
  2. Developing technical, economic, and financial feasibility studies for the subprojects, defining engineering and architectural alternatives, and estimating the construction, operation, and maintenance costs;
  3. Preparing preliminary engineering and architectural designs to serve as a robust basis for future detailed design and construction bidding documents;
  4. Preparing Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) and associated instruments, verifying compliance with national legislation and World Bank environmental and social standards, and validating proposed mitigation measures;
  5. Evaluating the national legal and regulatory framework relevant to land use, environmental licensing, and infrastructure development, identifying potential bottlenecks or risks, and providing advice and support to the PIU to address them;
  6. Preparing detailed preliminary technical specifications for the core infrastructure modules, covering civil works, solar photovoltaic energy, irrigation systems, and rural road rehabilitation, ensuring technical viability, climate resilience, and sustainability.

 

The expected duration of the consultancy contract will be 5 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Possess a minimum of 7 (seven) years of proven experience in preparing technical and economic feasibility studies and in developing preliminary projects for small and medium-scale infrastructure, preferably in the sectors of photovoltaic solar energy, irrigation systems, hydraulic ditches, rural access roads and rehabilitation of small road infrastructure;
  • Possess a minimum of 05 (five) years of proven experience in the preparation of environmental and social studies for infrastructure projects (including ESMPs and other applicable E&S instruments, proportionate to the risk and defined by subproject.), preferably in the sectors of photovoltaic solar energy, irrigation systems, hydraulic ditches, rural access roads and rehabilitation of small road infrastructures
  • Having performed at least 2 (two) tasks of a similar nature in the last 10 (ten) years, involving technical studies or preliminary projects for infrastructure to support local or productive development;
  • Proven experience in carrying out at least two (2) similar projects in Angola or comparable Portuguese-speaking countries, including knowledge of Presidential Decree No. 117/20 and applicable environmental licensing procedures, and involving environmental and social studies of projects and infrastructure to support local or productive development.
  • Demonstrate proven practical experience in preparing cost-benefit analyses, financial modeling, risk assessment, and market studies, including the development of sensitivity scenarios;
  • Demonstrate knowledge and experience in applying the standards and procedures of international financial institutions, namely the World Bank or equivalent multilateral entities, including requirements related to environmental and social safeguards, institutional analysis, and regulatory framework;
  • To demonstrate institutional capacity to operate effectively in multi-stakeholder contexts, ensuring strong technical coordination with public institutions, local authorities, and other relevant actors in Angola, while fostering meaningful engagement with local communities.
  • Possess a valid Environmental Consultancy certification issued by the Ministry of the Environment (MINAMB), proving your legal authorization to conduct environmental studies in Angola. The certification must be presented as part of the Technical Proposal and must be up-to-date at the time of submission.
  • Having established internal quality management and occupational health and safety systems, preferably certified according to ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 standards, or equivalent, will be considered an advantage.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0800 to 1600 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (only by mail) until August 27, 2026.

The address mentioned above is as follows:

Ministry of Planning
