      2. Company profile.
      3. Organisational structure.
      4. Quality assurance arrangements.
      5. Availability of key technical staff.
      6. Information on software, modelling tools and analytical capacity relevant to the assignment.

 

  1. The short-listing criteria are:
  1. Demonstrated experience in developing national clean cooking, energy transition or comparable energy sector strategies.
  2. Demonstrated experience in clean cooking technologies, markets, value chains and energy access planning.
  3. Experience in policy, regulatory and institutional analysis in the energy sector.
  4. Experience in undertaking household and institutional energy demand assessments, market analysis and consumer research.
  5. Demonstrated experience in investment planning, financial modelling, climate finance and carbon finance for energy access or clean cooking programmes.
  6. Demonstrated experience integrating gender equality, social inclusion and stakeholder engagement into energy sector assignments.
  7. Experience undertaking similar assignments in Sub-Saharan Africa, preferably Southern Africa.
  8. Experience working with governments, development partners or World Bank-financed projects.
  9.  Experience in developing women’s entrepreneurship programme frameworks, including business support models and financing/incubation pathways in the energy sector.
  1. Consultants may associate with other consultants to enhance their qualifications. Where firms are associating, the submission must include verifiable evidence of association from all parties. Experience and qualifications of parent or subsidiary firms will not be considered for evaluation.

Shortlisted Consultants will subsequently have their RFPs evaluated in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based (QCBS) selection method as per the seventh edition of Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025.

AVIS À MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

« SÉLECTION D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL NATIONAL POUR L’ÉVALUATION DES POINTS D’ENTRÉE (PoE) ET DES CENTRES DE SURVEILLANCE ÉPIDÉMIOLOGIQUE (CSE) »

 

  1. Contexte

 Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad, à travers le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Prévention, bénéficie de l’appui financier de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Projet [nom du Projet].

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités du Projet, il est prévu de renforcer les capacités nationales de prévention, de détection et de réponse aux menaces sanitaires, notamment à travers l’amélioration des capacités de surveillance épidémiologique et des capacités requises au niveau des Points d’Entrée (PoE), conformément aux exigences du Règlement sanitaire international (RSI, 2005).

À cet effet, le Projet envisage de recruter un Consultant Individuel National chargé de réaliser une évaluation exhaustive des capacités des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE).

  1. Objet de la mission

La mission consiste à réaliser une évaluation détaillée et documentée des capacités de l’ensemble des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE) concernés, afin d’identifier les capacités existantes, les insuffisances, les écarts par rapport aux exigences applicables, ainsi que les besoins prioritaires de renforcement.

Le consultant devra notamment effectuer des visites physiques sur l’ensemble des sites concernés et produire un rapport d’évaluation assorti d’un plan d’amélioration opérationnel et priorisé.

  1. Profil et qualifications requis

Le consultant devra notamment répondre aux exigences suivantes :

  • être titulaire au minimum d’un Master en santé publique, épidémiologie, médecine, santé internationale ou dans un domaine directement pertinent ;
  • justifier d’au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans les systèmes de surveillance épidémiologique ;
  • disposer d’une expérience avérée dans l’évaluation des systèmes de surveillance et/ou des systèmes de santé ;
  • disposer d’une expérience dans l’évaluation des capacités sanitaires des Points d’Entrée (PoE) ;
  • avoir une excellente connaissance du RSI (2005) ;
  • avoir une bonne maîtrise de la Surveillance Intégrée de la Maladie et la Riposte (SIMR) ;
  • disposer d’une expérience dans la préparation et la réponse aux urgences de santé publique ;
  • avoir une bonne capacité de collecte, de traitement et d’analyse des données ;
  • disposer d’excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et analytiques en français ;
  • maîtriser les outils bureautiques et les outils d’analyse et de traitement des données ;
  • avoir une bonne connaissance du contexte du système de santé et du dispositif national de surveillance épidémiologique du Tchad.
  • Une expérience de travail avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Prévention et/ou les structures nationales de surveillance constituera un avantage.
  1. Durée de la mission

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours calendaires.

La mission nécessitera des déplacements à N’Djaména ainsi que dans les provinces et localités où sont implantés les PoE et les CSE concernés par l’évaluation.

5. Méthode de sélection

Le consultant sera recruté conformément aux dispositions du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant un Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition septembre 2025, selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels (CI).

5. Dépôt des manifestations d’intérêt

Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française doivent être déposées sous pli fermé et/ou transmises par voie électronique à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous au plus tard le 10 septembre 2026 à 16 heures 00 (heure de N’Djamena), avec la mention :

« Manifestation d’Intérêt Sélection d’un Consultant Individuel National pour l’évaluation des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE)»

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – CONSULTANCY FIRM)

ALBANIA

Project: National Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Modernization Program (P4R)

TF No.: B8448

Assignment Title: Strategic Coastal Water Supply Framework and Feasibility Studies for Priority Water Supply Investments in the South Coast of Albania

Reference No.: AL-AKUK -329330-CS-QCBS

Albania is implementing governance and service reforms in the WSS sector supported by the World Bank through P4R project financed by SECO (Swiss Government). In parallel, structural reform changes are being launched by the government, including the creation of the new Water Production Operator (OPU) while the details of its future role and structure are still evolving; therefore this assignment shall focus on AKUK’s current mandate and existing institutional set-up, and reflect OPU-related interfaces only where and when formally clarified or necessary as working assumptions.

 

This Request for Expressions of Interest aims to assist AKUK in hiring a Consultant to prepare a Feasibility Study for potable water supply within the defined Project Area with a planning horizon extending to 2050, building upon the analyses, methodologies and strategic planning principles developed under the DWD DSIP and subsequent sector planning initiatives.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://akuk.gov.al/

The activities described in these TORs are expected to be completed within a period of 10 months, following the signing of the consultancy contract.

The consulting firm shall demonstrate proven experience in assignments of similar nature, including:

  • At least one (1) completed projects in strategic water supply planning, master planning, or system development studies;
  • At least one (1) assignments involving water resources assessment and supply-demand balance analysis;
  • At least one (1) projects including water demand forecasting based on demographic, tourism, and consumption scenarios;
  • At least one (1) assignment involving strategic assessment of water supply infrastructure alternatives;
  • At least one (1) project including economic and technical evaluation of alternatives;
  • At least one (1) project carried out for a water utility, public water operator, or public authority responsible for water services;
  • Experience in GIS-based infrastructure planning and spatial analysis.
  • Experience in projects implemented in tourism-intensive areas or comparable environments will be considered an asset.
  • Preference will be given to firms with experience in projects financed by International Financial Institutions (IFI) or European Union programmes.

The assignment shall be carried out by a multidisciplinary team. The indicative total input is of approximately sixty-five (65) person-months, reflecting the feasibility, environmental and social, and field investigation components. The core team shall include, at minimum:

  • Team Leader / Senior Water Supply Engineer;
  • Water Resources / Hydrogeologist;
  • Hydraulic Modelling Engineer;
  • Financial/Economic Analyst;
  • Environmental Specialist (P-ESIA);
  • Social Development Specialist (ESS5/ESS10);
  • GIS and Data Management Specialist;
  • Institutional/Utility Specialist;
  • Climate Resilience Specialist,

The proposed experts may be national and/or international, as appropriate for the assignment, and supported by additional experts, survey teams and field investigation activities. The Consultant shall justify the proposed allocation of expert inputs in its Technical Proposal. Please see criteria for the experts within ToRs document.

The evaluation criteria to be used for selecting the successful Consultant will be the following:

•           General Qualifications, including core business and years in business, (30 points);

•           Relevant experience, including previous experience in the field of assignment, (70 points);

The service will be selected under the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations), in investment project financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services November 2020, in accordance with Quality and Cost Based Selecton (QCBS), Lump-Sum Contract. The Bank requires that firms or individuals involved in Bank IPF procurement shall not have conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 16:00, Mondays to Thursdays, and from 08:00 to 14:00 on Fridays.

Expressions of interest (CV, Cover letter and documentary evidence for fulfilling the qualifications) must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail within September 10th, 2026.

Mrs. Elidjana Celaj

data.notice_text:
NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

The Executive Director

National Local Government Finance Committee

Area 14, Red Cross Building

Presidential Way

P.O. Box 31162

Lilongwe 3

Or through the following email address:

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw/ ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

Only shortlisted applicants will be considered for further assessments.

INVITACIÓN DE SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIÓNES DE INTERÉS SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORIA INDIVIDUAL

País: Honduras

Proyecto de Conectividad Sostenible de Honduras

Crédito: IDA-76720

Proyecto No. P181166

Consultoría Individual: COORDINADOR GENERAL

DE LA UNIDAD EJECUTORA DEL PROYECTO (UEP)

Referencia: HN-SIT-564200-CS-INDV

 

El Gobierno de la República de Honduras ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para el Proyecto de Conectividad Sostenible de Honduras y se propone utilizar una parte de los fondos para los contratos de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría (“los servicios”) que se pretenden contratar son: un consultor individual como Consultor COORDINADOR GENERAL DE LA UNIDAD EJECUTORA DEL PROYECTO (UEP), Los Términos de Referencia de esta asignación se encuentran publicados en la página web mencionada al final de esta solicitud, o podrán ser solicitados al Contratante a la dirección allí mencionada.

La Secretaría de Infraestructura y Transporte (SIT), invita a consultores individuales elegibles a expresar su interés en prestar los servicios solicitados. Los consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que indique que están cualificados para suministrar los servicios. Los criterios a evaluar para la selección son:

 PERFIL DEL CONSULTOR

Experiencia

1.  Profesional Universitario con grado de licenciatura en Ingeniería Civil.

2.  Maestría o cursos de especialización en Administración de Proyectos, Gestión de Proyectos, Finanzas, Gestión de Calidad o similares.

3.  Experiencia general de quince (15) años en el ejercicio de su profesión contadas a partir de la obtención de su título a nivel universitario.

4.  Experiencia mínima de diez (10) años en cargos de Gerente, Coordinador, Director o equivalente, de Componentes o Unidades administradoras, Firmas de Supervisión o Empresas Constructoras gestionando proyectos de infraestructura.

5.  Trayectoria comprobada en la gestión de al menos dos proyectos financiados por bancos multilaterales de desarrollo o donantes internacionales.

6.  Experiencia durante los últimos 10 años, desempeñando funciones de dirección en la Supervisión, ejecución como Contratista o Coordinación del Propietario en al menos tres (3) proyectos ejecutados de rehabilitación, construcción o mejoramiento de infraestructura vial pavimentada con montos de inversión superior a 20 millones de dólares por proyecto.

 

Habilidades y Competencias

  1. Sólidas habilidades de gestión de proyectos, incluida la planificación, presupuestación, monitoreo y evaluación.
  2. Excelentes habilidades analíticas y de resolución de problemas, con atención al detalle y capacidad para gestionar asignaciones complejas.
  3. Dominio del paquete Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) y software de gestión de proyectos.
  4. Habilidades efectivas de comunicación oral y escrita en español; se valorará el dominio del inglés.
  5. Capacidad para preparar informes técnicos y de avance de alta calidad.
  6. Sólidas habilidades interpersonales y capacidad demostrada para trabajar de manera colaborativa con diversos actores, incluidas agencias gubernamentales, comunidades locales y socios internacionales.
  7. Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y cumplir plazos ajustados.
  8. Compromiso con estándares éticos, transparencia y rendición de cuentas en la gestión de proyectos.

 

Las personas interesadas deberán detallar claramente en su hoja de vida su experiencia profesional y perfil académico, incluyendo el detalle de las funciones realizadas.

La expresión de interés de los consultores interesados, es requerida bajo el párrafo 7.34 de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión publicadas por el Banco Mundial septiembre 2023, que pueden encontrarse en el sitio web www.worldbank.org. De igual forma, se señala a la atención de los consultores interesados la Sección III Gobernanza, párrafos, 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17 que establece el Banco Mundial conflicto de interés.

Los Consultores serán seleccionados en base al método Selección Abierta y Competitiva de Consultores Individuales descrito en las Regulaciones antes mencionada. Los consultores interesados pueden obtener más información en la dirección indicada al final de esta publicación, durante horas hábiles de 9:00 a.m. a 05:00 p.m. hasta el 07 de septiembre del 2026.

Las expresiones de interés y su documentación deberán ser recibidas en físico en las oficinas de la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto del Banco Mundial o por correo a la dirección indicada a continuación bm@sit.gob.hn a más tardar el 11 de septiembre del año 2026 hasta las 4:00 pm.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST
Country: Republic of Tajikistan
Project name: Tajikistan Digital Foundations Project
Project number: P506611
Grant No. TF-C6744
Implementation agency: State Institution "Projects Implementation Center Fundamentals of Digitalization in Tajikistan" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan
State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan is implementing Tajikistan Digital Foundation Project (thereafter referred to as Project) co-financed by the World Bank and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC).
The objective of the Project is to improve the delivery of digitally-enabled public services and to enhance the digital skills of the population. The Project development objective is to expand access to and usage of selected digital public services and enhance digital skills of the population. The project consists of two main components designed to leverage digital technologies for both social objectives (i.e., inclusive access to public services) and economic objectives (job creation and economic growth), as follows:
Component 1. Strengthening Foundations for Safe Digital Government Systems and Services.
Component 2. Enhancing Digital Skills.
To support the implementation of the planned activities the PIC EOP intends to hire Devops Engineer Expert
The objective of this assignment is to ensure the reliable, secure, scalable, and efficient operation of the OJSC’s server and DevOps infrastructure by embedding modern DevOps practices and leading a structured, assessment-led modernisation of the infrastructure that supports public service delivery.

The Terms of Reference for the assignment can be found at the following link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/16EbNXVu7z58S8yuysveukKCq16Au41n4/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=115133111040801685890&rtpof=true&sd=true 
Qualification requirements for candidates are as follow:
    Bachelor’s degree (minimum) in IT, computer science, computer engineering, or related field. Master’s degree or relevant certifications (e.g. CKA/CKAD, cloud or security) an asset.
    Minimum three (3) years in DevOps engineering or systems administration; five (5) + years and senior-level experience is desirable.
    Proven operation/maintenance of production environments at scale, including high availability, backup/recovery, and capacity management.
    Strong hands-on Linux administration: configuration, hardening, performance tuning, troubleshooting.
    Demonstrated experience designing, building, and operating containerized workloads with Docker, including image standardization.
    Working knowledge of container orchestration concepts required; hands-on production experience with Kubernetes (deployment, scaling, cluster operations) is an advantage and may be strengthened during the assignment’s assessment phase.
    Demonstrated experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines with automated build, test, deployment, and rollback.
    Working knowledge of modern infrastructure-automation and infrastructure-as-code tooling for version-controlled provisioning.
    Experience implementing and operating monitoring, alerting, and centralized logging/observability platforms.
    Sound networking knowledge: configuration, segmentation, DNS/domain administration, and TLS/SSL certificate management.
    Solid grasp of information-security principles: access management, hardening, patching, secrets management, and compliance.
    Working knowledge of cloud and/or virtualized infrastructure; able to operate hybrid or on-premises environments.
    Ability to produce high-quality technical documentation, assessments, plans, and reports for technical and management audiences.
    Experience operating government or large-enterprise digital systems is desirable.
    Experience on donor-funded projects (World Bank, ADB, UNDP, EU) desirable; Central Asia or comparable context an asset.
    Professional working Russian required; working English required for documentation/reporting; Tajik an asset.
State Institution "Projects Implementation Center Fundamentals of Digitalization in Tajikistan" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan now invites eligible consultants (Individual consultant) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (CV, copy of documents evidencing appropriate qualifications and skills, experience and competence related to the task, description of similar tasks performed, references, etc).   
The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (July 2016, revised in September 2023) - Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the selection of Individual Consultants (IC) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines. 
Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 17:00 hours of Dushanbe, Tajikistan time. 
Expressions of interest must be delivered to the address below by September 11, 2026 (17:00 p.m.)

1.0 Background

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Monitoring & Evaluation Officer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Monitoring & Evaluation Officer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Monitoring & Evaluation Officer are as follows:

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of M&E officer position is to assist in ensuring the effective, efficient and transparent management in supporting evidence-based Project Monitoring and Evaluation for GESD 2.0. Further, ensuring that Project objectives and activities are achieved in strict compliance with existing legislation, combined with the management standards set out in world bank procedures.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Develop, operationalize, and maintain the project's Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework, including indicators, targets, data collection tools, and reporting systems.
  2. Coordinate the collection, verification, analysis, and management of project data from all implementing entities and participating Local Authorities.
  3. Monitor progress against the Project Development Objective (PDO), Results Framework, annual work plans, and performance indicators, and provide timely feedback to management.
  4. Prepare monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual project performance reports in accordance with project reporting requirements, including leveraging data from the Project Management Information System (PMIS).
  5. Conduct data quality assessments and verification exercises to ensure the accuracy, completeness, reliability, and timeliness of project data.
  6. Support the development of annual work plans and budgets by providing performance data, trend analysis, and evidence-based recommendations.
  7. Coordinate baseline studies, mid-term reviews, beneficiary assessments, impact evaluations, and end-of-project evaluations as required.
  8. Monitor implementation progress at both central and local government levels through field visits, supervision missions, and performance reviews.
  9. Prepare periodic Results Framework performance reports showing progress towards achievement of project targets and indicators.
  10. Support the preparation and organization of World Bank implementation support missions, project reviews, and other monitoring missions by providing relevant data and analytical reports.
  11. Develop scorecards, and other performance monitoring tools to facilitate evidence-based decision-making.
  12. Document lessons learned, best practices, success stories, and implementation challenges to support knowledge management and continuous improvement.
  13. Build the capacity of project staff, Local Authorities, and other stakeholders in monitoring, evaluation, results-based management, and reporting.
  14. Ensure that monitoring and evaluation activities comply with project requirements, Government policies, and donor reporting standards.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

  1. Master’s Degree in Economics, Statistics or Demography; an advanced training in Monitoring and Evaluation will be considered an added advantage.
  2. Minimum of five (5) years of relevant working experience in an M&E position.
  3. Experience in data collection, data analysis, reporting, communication and project management.
  4. Demonstrated Computer Skill (Proficiency in using computer desktop application MS Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint); and fair knowledge of Statistical Packages such as SPSS and Stata.
  5. Experience in designing, implementing and operating project M&E systems from project initiation to close out stages.
  6. Experience in designing and managing beneficiary monitoring and database systems.
  7. Experience in strategic planning and performance measurement, including indicator selection, target setting, reporting, database management and developing M&E and performance monitoring plans.
  8. Demonstrated working knowledge of the major evaluation methodologies (such as qualitative, quantitative, mixed-method and impact) and data collection and analysis methodologies.
  9. Experience in planning and managing surveys.
  10. Experience in developing and refining data collection tools, quality assessments and oversight.
  11. Ability to mainstream gender in monitoring and evaluation of projects or programmes.
  12. Ability to work in a team and good interpersonal skills, result oriented; proactive and attention to detail.
  13. Self-starter and ability to work under minimal supervision.

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The M&E Officer will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The M&E Officer will occasionally be required to travel to all local government authorities in Malawi where the GESD 2.0 Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation (M&E).

 

7.REPORTING

The Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will report to the Project Coordinator. S/he shall work in corroboration with the monitoring and evaluation team of the NLGFC.

 

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Individual Consultant- Occupational Health and Safety Specialist

No: MW-NLGFC-563903-CS-INDIV

                     

                                         Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

 

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Occupational Health and Safety Specialist on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Occupational Health and Safety Specialist tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Occupational Health and Safety Specialist are as follows:

 

The Objectives of the Assignment

The main aim of this assignment is to ensure that all OHS risks and impacts are managed in accordance with national Occupational Health and Safety Policies and framework, World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP). Working with other team members, the Occupational Health and Safety Specialist will ensure the implementation of the project’s occupational health and safety safeguards instruments, monitor compliance by project implementers and report progress in all the 28 district and 4 municipal local authorities.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Considering World Bank Environmental Health Safety Guidelines (EHSG), Good International Industry Practice (GIIP), compile OHS procedures update where applicable the OHS strategy, system and the operational plans for the district led subcomponent which falls under the National Local Government Finance Committee PIU;
  2. Together with OHS officers of contractors, develop, update, coordinate and facilitate the development and/or revision of and OHS risk assessments and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for the various activities under the applicable activities of the Project;
  3. Liaise with other specialists (including Environmental, Social, Project Engineer, etc.) in the team on OHS matters to review severe OHS incidents, recurring minor incidents, and near misses that have occurred on project with the aim to further mitigate these from repeating;
  4. Facilitate the development of Health and Safety Manual and a health and Safety Management plan for the local authorities implemented project activities and incorporate the relevant OHS measures (including emergency preparedness and response measures) into the Labour Management Procedures (LMP) and community Safety;
  5. Conducting Occupational Health Safety site inspections on a regular basis with adequate frequency;
  6. Identify potential hazards to project workers and community members;
  7. Ensure preventive and protective measures, including modification, substitution, or elimination of hazardous conditions or substances;
  8. Ensure applicable protective equipment to protect against residual risks is provided;
  9. Providing internal audits on Occupational Health and Safety issues all project sites implemented by local authorities;
  10. Facilitating wellness health awareness and screening Programs in all the local authorities;
  11. Ensure training requirements for project workers, and where necessary community members, are included, and training records are maintained;
  12. Support project teams and clients in investigating the root cause/s of the incidents and developing appropriate remedial and mitigation measures;
  13. Prepare and deliver reports to the project on OHS incidents, patterns of incidents, and proposed recommendations;
  14. Develop and implement a comprehensive intervention to improve worker OHS, and Community Health and Safety for communities directly impacted by the project;
  15. Develop and implement a training program on Occupational Health and Safety for local authorities and contractors; and maintain training records;
  16. Document and report occupational accidents, diseases and incidents;
  17. Recommend measures to help protect workers, and community members, from potentially hazardous work methods, working at heights, scaffolding measures, working adjacent to flowing water, hazardous substances and waste management and disposal, and other relevant processes, or materials;
  18. Advise communities and/or institutions/local authorities regarding health or safety issues;
  19. Inspect or evaluate workplace environments, equipment, or practices to ensure compliance with safety standards and government regulations;
  20. Develop or maintain hygiene programs, such as noise surveys, continuous atmosphere monitoring, ventilation surveys, or asbestos management plans;
  21. Document and report on job hazard assessments, identified mitigation measures, permits to work, standard operating procedures developed to carry out work safely based on Job Hazard Assessment (JHA) and Permission To Work (PTW), all incidents or near misses, use of first aid kits, tool box talks, training programme for workers, labour procedures, signed codes of conduct by all persons working on or visiting the site, contracts of all workers, activity ESMP, Contractors ESMP, any permits for the work or resources used for the work, etc.;
  22. Describe emergency prevention and preparedness and response arrangements to emergency situations, and report significant incidents to the LG PIU and World Bank within 48 hours;
  23. Review and inputs into community emergency procedure plans for subcomponent activities;
  24. Propose remedies for adverse impacts such as occupational injuries, deaths, disability and disease;
  25. Inspect work environments to ensure safety for the workers and community in all project sites;
  26. Conduct safety training or education programs, job hazard assessments, and demonstrate the use of safety equipment, and maintain training records;
  27. Investigate health-related complaints and inspect facilities to ensure that they comply with public health legislation and regulations, and World Bank’s ESF and ESHS requirements, and project ESMF;
  28. Develop or maintain medical monitoring programs for employees and contractors;
  29. Set up monitoring systems for the sites, including file management on site for Toolbox talks and topics, ongoing skills and training development, SOPs, permits to work, incident reports, monitoring First Aid kits, etc. Ensuring first aid kits are appropriately stocked to type of activities anticipated on sites, etc;
  30. Develop and review and monitoring emergency procedures for sites including ensuring correct fire prevent controls and training in place, etc;
  31. Coordinate “right-to-know” programs regarding hazardous chemicals or other substances, and safety procedure;
  32. Maintain or update Emergency Response Plans or procedures, as well as waste management plan, traffic safety management plan, hazardous substances management plan, etc., with necessary SOPs or safety procedures developed in the OHS strategy and plan; and
  33. Apply ESS4 to anticipate and avoid adverse impacts on the health and safety of project-affected communities during the project life cycle from both routine and non-routine circumstances, including to avoid or minimize community expose to project-related traffic and road safety risks, diseases and hazardous materials, effective measures to address emergency events, and ensure safeguarding of personnel and property is carried out in a manner that avoids or minimizes risks to the project affected communities.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. Master’s Degree in disciplines such as Engineering (Civil, Electrical, Environmental, Quality and Safety), Environmental Health and Safety.
  2. A qualification and or international certificate in OHS such as NEBOSH, or similar.
  3. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience in developing, implementing and/or supervising OHS in construction, with experience in transport infrastructure, energy, hydropower, DRM and or extractives sectors.
  4. Knowledge of OHS management systems, including experience auditing/ assessing health and safety programs and systems.
  5. Membership of professional bodies and experience in implementing World Bank funded projects and/or other multilateral banks’ OHS policies will be an added advantage.
  6. Demonstrated ability to assess technical issues of occupational health and safety and to effect a cultural change to create a culture of safety across a workplace or organization
  7. Have excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills
  8. Proficiency in using computer applications e.g. MS Word, Excel and Power Point.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The OHS Specialist will be based at the National Local Government Finance Committee Head Office in Lilongwe. The OHS Specialist will be required to travel to district authorities and to project sites in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

7.REPORTING

The Occupational Health and Safety Specialist will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social Economic Services at the NLGFC for technical matters and will work in collaboration with local authorities and other specialists under the project; Environmental Safeguards Specialist, Social Safeguards Specialist, and Project Engineers.

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS) on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS) tenable at the NLGFC Offices.

 

The terms of Reference (TORs) for Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Environnmental Safeguard Specilaist will ensure that GESD 2.0 activities comply with the Worlad Bank ESF and ESH guidelines as outlined in the governing Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), and Project Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) including all the supporting management plans as appropriate

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. coordination and provision of technical supervision, monitor and report on Environment safeguards in line with the national laws and in conformity with the Environmental and Social Framework of the World Bank and international best practices under the project;
  2. Provision of preventive and protective measures, including modification, substitution, or elimination of environmental risks and impacts; and
  3. Design and development of training programme for district officers, contractors and workers etc.
  4. Support the eligible local authorities in conducting environmental and social screening followed by the timely development and disclosure of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) of all sub-project activities implemented by local authorities with the aim of incorporating due processes as standard practice in social and environmental safeguards implementation;
  5. Conduct reviews of ESMPs of all the subprojects developed by the local authorities in compliance with Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), RAPs, and other relevant E and S instruments to ensure quality and timely submission;
  6. Provide and review environmental and social inputs into the planning, design and contracting of investments, including the preparation of tender documents in line with the Environmental and Social Frameworks (ESF);
  7. Develop and implement an internal administrative tracking system for the PIU in order to monitor the progress of project activities in terms of meeting environmental and social safeguard requirements. The system will include the planning, assessment, approval, implementation and monitoring phases of GESD 2.0 Project activities. The system will be computer based (using a spread sheet or Microsoft Access) and designed for easy data entry and report generation. Reports generated by the system should be simple to produce, showing progress of a specific project activity, and highlight critical items such as pending or overdue actions;
  8. Design and deliver, or arrange for the delivery of, an environmental and social safeguards capacity building program for local authorities’ staff and other relevant stakeholders with the purpose of strengthening capacity of local authorities to implement environmental and social safeguard requirements effectively within the context of larger GESD 2.0 activities;
  9. Following up implementation of environmental screening and implementation of ESMPs and Social response operations at sector and district levels through EDOs (local authority staff);
  10. Undertaking review of CESMPs and provide feedback to local authorities;
  11. Undertake spots checks on compliance monitoring of Contractors Environmental and Social Management Plan for PBG sub-projects;
  12. Undertaking site visits and reviewing contractors' compliance with site-specific CESMPs, Labour Management Procedures (LMPs), Codes of Conducts etc. including determining and suggesting remedial actions in collaboration with the Environmental Expert and Occupational Safety and Health (OHS) Expert;
  13. Preparation of non-compliance reports and keeping track of respective responses/actions undertaken and preparation of periodic Environmental Compliance Monitoring Reports;
  14. Participating at the official meetings with the Bank and other forums related to the project;
  15. Undertake internal E&S Audits and support consultants in the preparation of external E&S Audits, and track the implementation of the corrective and remedial action plans by the district and municipal councils;
  16. Provide inputs and materials to Communication Specialist for devising communication strategy, knowledge products and dissemination of results;
  17. Timely preparation and submission of monthly, quarterly, annual and period reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and World Bank task team; and
  18. Performing any other duties as may be necessary for the effective implementation of the project as assigned by Project Coordinator and or Director of Social and Economic Services.

 

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. Master’s Degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources Management, Environmental Policy and Analysis; Environmental Management and Economics;
  2. A minimum of 8 years of experience in the field of environmental management at National level or international organization, and donor projects handling environmental and social aspects of planning, assessing and managing civil works projects of various scale in Malawi or similar African countries;
  3. Working knowledge of World Bank environmental and social frameworks, especially Environmental and Social Assessment (ESS1), Land Acquisition, Restriction on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement (ESS5), and have demonstrated experience in successfully preparing ESIAs, ESMPs and RAPs in line with World Bank standards, policies will be considered an advantage;
  4. Working knowledge of regulations in Malawi related to Environmental and Social issues;
  5. Experience with designing and delivering capacity building programs;
  6. Familiarity with Article VI of Paris 21 Agreement; environmental, social and economic conditions prevailing in Malawi or similar African countries;
  7. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills;
  8. Strong organizational and communications skills and ability to interface with grassroots, district and sector players in the discipline;
  9. Demonstrated Computer Skill (Proficiency in using computer desktop application MS Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint);
  10. Knowledge of the decentralized local government systems in Malawi; and
  11. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The Contract is for a period of 3 years with yearly review. The renewal of the contract is upon satisfactory appraisal results.

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will occasionally be required to travel to all local government authorities in Malawi where the GESD 2.0 Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation (environmental safeguards).

7.REPORTING

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Financial Management Specialist (FMS) tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Financial Management Specialist (FMS) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the Financial Management Specialist position is to ensure the sound financial management of the project in compliance with the Financing Agreement, Government of Malawi public financial management regulations, including the Public Finance Management Act and related regulations, treasury instructions and IFMIS desk instructions, project operations manual, and World Bank financial management requirements. The Financial Management Specialist will be responsible for planning, budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, funds management, audit coordination, and financial compliance to ensure that project resources are used efficiently, effectively, transparently, and for their intended purposes.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Preparation of Financial Statements in accordance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) of the Project within six months from the end of the financial year; 
  2. Coordination of the preparation of a consolidated project budget, cash flow forecasts, execution and monitoring including liaising with key ministries and departments for budget planning and execution;

  7. Ensure that all necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts with physical documents have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statement of Expenditures (SOE) or Interim Financial Reports (IFRs) methods of reporting.
  8. Periodically review the performance of control functions to ensure that internal controls are sufficient and functioning correctly and that Financial Performance of the Project is Satisfactory;

  12. Advise the Project Coordinator and Director of Finance on all financial and control considerations of the project;

  15. Undertake all other duties and responsibilities commensurate with the role and level of this position as may be requested by the Project Coordinator.

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Procurement Specialist on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Procurement Specialist at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Procurement Specialist are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of the Procurement Specialist is to ensure that all goods, works, consulting services, and non-consulting services required for project implementation are procured efficiently, transparently, economically, and in compliance with applicable procurement regulations and donor requirements.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Coordinate the preparation and updating of Project’s Annual Procurement Plan;
  2. Prepare the General Procurement Notices (GPN), and Specific Procurement Notices (SPN), and Solicitations of Expression of Interests (SEOI), when required;
  3. Preparation of solicitation Documents such as request For bids, request for proposals and request For quotations for goods for procurement of goods, works, consulting and non-consulting services.
  4. Manage evaluation of bids/proposals/quotations including managing contract negotiation meetings;
  5. Updating the World Bank Procurement Tracking System for monitoring of the Project procurement activities (STEP) for NLGFC and Local Authorities including seeking “No Objection”, from the World Bank for the Procurement Plan and other stages in case of all procurements.
  6. Ensure that STEP is updated and used in real time for the local authorities;
  7. Preparation of evaluation reports, contracts, award notices and other procurement and contractual documents as required;
  8. Establish and maintain procedures for the receiving, inspecting, testing and acceptance of goods;
  9. Ensure compliance with procurement methods and prior review thresholds applicable to the Project;
  10. Ensure all procurement activities are carried out in accordance with the agreed procedures, including the Financing Agreement; the World Bank Procurement Guidelines/regulations; and Government of Malawi Public Procurement and Disposal of Assets Act 2025, where applicable;
  11. Assist in timely payments to suppliers, and consultants and also ensuring their contractual obligations such as payment guarantees, Insurance premiums and performance Bonds;
  12. Establish and Maintain a contract management plan covering all infrastructures, sub components under GESD 2.0 across all participating councils to monitor contractor performance against milestones and advice on contract modifications and claims, including but not limited to variations, extensions, dispute resolutions and completion certificates
  13. Establish and maintain a central procurement filing system, and ensure all related documents are included in the respective files (physically and electronically);
  14. Establish a performance monitoring database for all suppliers and consultants, and ensure timely updates of the system;
  15. Preparation and timely submission Bid Evaluation Repots; and Monthly Procurement Plan Implementation Status Reports for submission to the World Bank.
  16. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual procurement progress reports for the PIT / Project Coordinator, aligned/coordinated with the work plan, to be submitted to NLGFC and the World Bank task team monthly/quarterly/annually.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. BSc in Procurement/Supply Chain/Logistics Management; or Bachelor of Business Administration/Management; or Professional Procurement/ Logistic/ Supply Chain Qualification  
  2. Master’s Degree in Procurement/Supply Chain/Logistics; or Master of Business Administration/Management;
  3. A minimum of eight (8) years of experience in procurement management in the public sector;
  4. Working knowledge of the Government of Malawi’s Public Procurement laws, regulations and procedures;
  5. Proven leadership and mentoring skills and evidence of ability to improve procurement performance;
  6. Proven ability to work under tight deadlines, and excellent team skills, including in multi-sectoral teams;
  7. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  8. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and   interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy;
  9. Membership of professional bodies like MIPS or CIPS-UK is considered an asset;
  10. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English;
  11. Proficiency in using computer applications e.g. MS Word, Excel and Power Point; and
  12. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The Contract is for a period of 3 years with yearly review. The renewal of the contract is upon satisfactory appraisal results.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Procurement Specialist (Consultant) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Procurement Specialist (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with procurement teams to guide and improve project implementation as it concerns procurement

7.REPORTING

The Procurement Specialist (Consultant) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Head of Procurement at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ Procurement Officers for the GESD 2.0 project.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      

                            Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Coordinator

No: MW-NLGFC-563879-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

 

  1. Introduction Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Project Coordinator on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Project Coordinator at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Project Coordinator are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the Project Coordinator position is to provide strategic leadership and day-to-day management of the project to ensure the timely and effective delivery of project activities and achievement of project objectives. The Project Coordinator will coordinate planning, budgeting, procurement, contract administration, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, human resource management, governance arrangements, stakeholder engagement, and implementation support missions, while ensuring compliance with Government and donor requirements.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Coordination: Ensure cross-component and cross-institutional coordination and linkages through information sharing, joint implementation of project activities and provide strategic guidance and coordination to the PIT members on all project related activities in order to keep workflow on track;

 

  1. Planning: Spearhead and coordinate the preparation and implementation of Project’s Annual Procurement Plan in line with agreed timelines and budgets; spearhead the planning and implementation of project activities to each activity specific goals and project goals overall in coordination with the PIT technical specialists and relevant key stakeholders; ensure that detailed activity plans are prepared and monitored; be proactive and provide solutions to bring forward delayed/off-track activities; ensure alignment of all activities with the annual work plan and budget;  

 

  1. Budgeting: Lead the timely development of consolidated project budgets for planned activities, cash flow forecasts, executing and monitoring of budgets, and ensure that the activity budgets are aligned with the annual work plan and consistent; coordinate with the PIT Financial Management Specialist and liaise with key ministries and departments and local authorities for budget planning and execution;

 

  1. Procurement: In coordination with the PIT Procurement Specialist ensure the timely preparation, execution and updated of procurement plans at the central level and at the district level; liaise with all relevant stakeholders; ensure that all procurements for consultants, goods and works under each procurement plan are carried out in accordance with the agreed procedures, including the Financing Agreement; the World Bank Procurement Guidelines/regulations and the Government of Malawi Public Procurement and Disposal of Assets Act 2025 and World Bank policies.

 

  1. Contract Management: Lead the management of contracts for consultants and other service providers, and work with all PIT members to evaluate potential problems and technical hitches and timely develop solutions;

 

  1. Financial Management: Manage financial resources of the project in coordination with the PIT Financial Management Specialist; ensure that all project activities are executed in accordance with the Financing Agreements, and the policies and standards of all relevant implementing agencies; ensure strict adherence to project budgets by monitoring expenses and implementing cost-saving measures; and ensure the timely preparation of financial statements and audits according to the Financing Agreement; ensure that the project is timely audited by the National Audit Office and submit an annual audit report to Government of Malawi and World Bank  not later than 30th September.

 

  1. Environmental and Social Safeguards: Ensure that all environment and social safeguards are adhered in all activities financed by the GESD 2.0 project and are managed in accordance with World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP); coordinate with relevant PIT specialists, district officials and relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies to ensure eligible local authorities develop and implements environmental safeguards issues in all the sub project sites;

 

  1. Project Office Management and Staff Management: Manage the PIT on a day-to-day basis; coordinate and supervise administrative activities necessary for the successful implementation of GESD 2.0; supervise and be responsible for the specialists’ time commitment and performance on the project; ensure timely preparation and submission of all consultants reports from the Project Engineers; Financial Management Specialist; Procurement Specialist; Monitoring and Evaluation Officer; Safeguards Specialist; Occupation and Health Specialist; Environmental Safeguard Specialist and all implementing agencies; undertake staff performance appraisals with support from  NLGFC; and

 

  1. Oversight Meetings, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Supervision: Facilitate key project meetings (quarterly project progress meetings, meetings of the Project Steering Committee, meetings of the Project Technical Committee) and liaison with stakeholders regularly and submit minutes of respective meetings within 48 hours; serve as Secretary to the PTC and supervise and ensure execution of any decisions approved by the PTC; ensure that all activities at central and at district level are carried out according to the provisions of the Malawi Government legislation and as stipulated in the Project Operations Manual and Financing Agreement; prepare and submit monthly, quarterly and annual project progress reports to the Executive Director and the World Bank task team; prepare and submit bi-annual updates on project progress against the project results framework; organize World Bank implementation support missions, including follow up on mission recommendations.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. A Master's Degree in Project Management, Economics, Development Studies, Finance/Accounting, Business Administration, or Engineering from a recognized institution;
  2. At least 8 years relevant working experience in senior positions or project management positions in public sector projects with a focus on planning, budget management and execution;
  3. At least 5 years of relevant working experience with Malawi’s Public Financial Management Structures; experience in fiscal decentralization is considered an asset;
  4. Demonstrated proficiency with project and budget management software / tracking tools, project fiduciary procedures;
  5. Demonstrated problem-solving skills and managerial skills, including proactivity;
  6. Demonstrated experience to work effectively with and in multi-sectoral teams;
  7. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  8. Highly motivated with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy;
  9. Experience in working with the World Bank, multi-lateral development partners or bilateral partners is considered an asset;
  10. Willingness to work under pressure, tight timelines, and with minimum supervision;
  11. Excellent communication and report writing skills and be fluent in English; and
  12. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Project Coordinator will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Coordinator will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

7.REPORTING

The Project Coordinator will report to the Executive Director of National Local Government Finance Committee for all the project progress and implementation issues.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.
