data.notice_text:
The State of Santa Catarina is in the process of contracting a loan operation with the World Bank to finance the SC Protected and Resilient Program, with part of the resources allocated for the procurement of specialized consulting services.

Within the scope of this procurement, the services comprise the hiring of a specialized consulting firm to prepare a detailed technical assessment, strategic planning, technical specifications, and a governance model aimed at structuring an integrated system for hydrometeorological observation, forecasting, and dissemination of information for the member States of the Council for the Development and Integration of the South – CODESUL (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Paraná, and Mato Grosso do Sul). The initiative aims to strengthen regional capacity for monitoring, forecasting, and issuing alerts related to extreme hydrometeorological events.

The estimated period for the execution of the services is 10 (ten) months, counted from the contract signing date, with the procurement process expected to begin in December 2026, in accordance with the provisions established in the respective Terms of Reference (ToR).

The details of the services and procurement requirements are described in the Terms of Reference (ToR) attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. The State Secretariat for Civil Protection and Defense of Santa Catarina invites qualified consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services under this procurement. Interested firms shall submit information demonstrating that they possess the technical qualifications, institutional experience, and operational capacity required for the proper execution of the Services, including the following requirements:

Experience in Similar Projects

Mandatory requirement: the firm shall have executed, within the last 10 (ten) years, at least 1 (one) project involving the following element:

  • Integration or development of hydrometeorological monitoring systems at the regional, national, or international level.

Desirable requirements: the firm shall have executed, within the last 10 (ten) years, projects involving the following elements:

  • Strategic planning or technical advisory services for national or state meteorological and/or hydrological services (National Meteorological Services, meteorological institutes, water agencies);
  • Technical specification and/or supervision of the implementation of early warning systems for natural disasters (floods, landslides, droughts, storms);
  • Consulting services for the modernization of information technology infrastructure applied to large volumes of environmental or scientific data;
  • Design of multi-institutional or multi-level governance models for shared information systems;
  • Diagnosis, assessment, or recommendations for meteorological, hydrological, or environmental observation networks
  • International experience demonstrating the capacity to operate in different institutional contexts and alignment with global best practices. Experience in projects financed by multilateral development banks, projects for international organizations, and/or initiatives conducted in multiple countries or within the framework of international technical cooperation will be considered.

Institutional Capacity

Mandatory requirement: The firm shall demonstrate institutional capacity through AT LEAST ONE of the following options:

Option A — Proven Consulting Experience and Mobilization Capacity: Certificate of at least 1 (one) relevant strategic or technical consulting project executed within the last 10 (ten) years (which may be the same project submitted under the Similar Projects Experience Requirement, if applicable).

Option B — Strategic Institutional Partnership: letter of support or formal partnership agreement with an institution of recognized national or international expertise in the fields of meteorology, hydrology, disaster risk management, or related areas, such as:

  • INPE (National Institute for Space Research);
  • INMET (National Institute of Meteorology);
  • Regional Centers of the WMO (World Meteorological Organization);
  • Leading universities with recognized programs in relevant fields;
  • National Meteorological and Hydrological Services or Institutes from other countries;
  • Research centers specialized in climate, water resources, or disaster management

Desirable requirements:

  • Meet Options A and B;
    • ISO 9001 (Quality Management System);
  • Quality Certifications – relevant and valid quality certifications, such as:
    • CMMI Level 3 or higher (Capability Maturity Model Integration);
    • Other recognized and equivalent international certifications.

The short list shall comprise a minimum of 5 (five) and a maximum of 8 (eight) selected consulting firms.

Interested Firms are hereby drawn attention to the provisions set forth in Section III, paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17, of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 edition, which address the policies applicable to conflicts of interest and unfair competitive advantage in procurement processes financed by the institution.

Firms may associate with other firms in order to complement their qualifications and technical capabilities and shall clearly indicate, in their Expression of Interest, whether such association will take the form of a joint venture and/or subcontracting arrangement. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the full performance of the contract, should the proposal be selected.

The Firm shall be selected in accordance with the applicable procurement procedures established in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 edition, and pursuant to the provisions set forth in the Request for Proposals (RFP).

Additional information may be obtained through the following email address comissaobird@sea.sc.gov.br by consulting the attached Terms of Reference, available on the website https://compras.sc.gov.br/sou-fornecedor.

Expressions of Interest shall be submitted exclusively by electronic means to the Contracting Committee, via the email address comissaobird@sea.sc.gov.br, by 7:00 p.m., Brasília time, on September 11, 2026, with the subject line: “EoI Nº 534/2026 – name of the interested party”.

REPUBLIC OF MALAWI

MINISTRY OF ENERGY

DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AFFAIRS

 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES –FIRM SELECTION)

Country:  Malawi

Project Name     :ASCENT Malawi Project

Project Number :P502464

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Design, Development and Implementation of Carbon Mitigation and Carbon Financing Activities in the Energy Sector

Reference No. :  MW-MOE.-550566-CS-QCBS

EOI Issue Date :  3rd August 2026

This request for expression of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for this Project that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) on 31st January 2025.

The Government of the Republic of Malawi through the Ministry of Energy has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) and Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) towards the cost of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Malawi (ASCENT Malawi) Project. It is intended that part of the proceeds of the financing will be used to cover eligible payments under the contracts for Consultancy services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) intent is to engage a qualified consulting firm to provide consultancy services to the Ministry of Energy (MOE), for the design, development and implementation of carbon mitigation and carbon financing activities in the energy sector, with a pilot for clean cooking solutions (CCS), in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. The firm consultant will provide analytical, advisory and process support including preparing required documentation to (i) support the GOM quantifiably determine the potential for emission reductions (ERs) in its current and potential energy sector investments, and the potential for generating, certifying and monetizing the ERs, across multiple technologies, scales and types; and (ii) pilot an ERs (sub)activity for clean cooking solutions under ASCENT Malawi completing full carbon financing cycle(s).

The assignment will cover the entire energy sector including at individual project levels such as ASCENT Malawi where the GOM seeks to raise carbon finance under Components 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the Project.

The objective of the assignment is to support the Government of Malawi, particularly the Ministry of Energy, in the design, development, operationalization, and implementation of carbon mitigation and carbon financing activities within the energy sector.

The scope of work under this assignment shall include the following, but not limited to:

  • Carbon Financing Modalities and Framework Development
  • Carbon Mitigation Activity Design and Registration
  • Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV)
  • Carbon Credit Issuance and Commercialization
  • Clean Cooking Carbon Finance Pilot
  • Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement

The detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) for the assignment can be found at the following websites: Ministry of Energy and Mining (https://energy.gov.mw/resources/), Ngwee Ngwee Ngwee Fund (https://www.nnnf.energy.gov.mw/resources/) and ASCENT Malawi Project (https://www.ascent.mw/resources/) or upon request through the following email address amopiha@ascent.mw copy to info@ascent.mw and austin.theu@energy.gov.mw. All requests for clarification should be sent through above emails, and the Client will respond to the requested clarifications.

The MoE now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm(s) and years in business of not less than Seven (7) years
  2. Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the below:
  • Experience in, and understanding of, the renewable energy and clean cooking market in sub-Saharan Africa, with preference for experience in East or Southern Africa;
  • Demonstrated experience applying household energy or clean cooking carbon methodologies under any of the following: Verra VM0050 or predecessor VMR0006 and VMR0011; Gold Standard TPDDTEC; Gold Standard Improved Cook Stove methodology; CDM AMS-II.G; GCCNMT016; or CLEAR Methodology;
  • Experience preparing PoAs and/or PDDs for clean cooking or energy access projects, of which at least two PoAs were successfully registered;
  • Demonstrated experience in successful registration of carbon projects under recognized standards (e.g., VCS, Gold Standard, CDM, Article 6), preferably including programmatic approaches such as PoAs
  • Proven experience with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, including knowledge of Corresponding Adjustments, NDC accounting, and Letter of Authorisation processes;
  • Proven experience conducting KPT, CCT, and WBT tests, and designing statistical sampling frameworks for carbon projects at scale;
  • Experience with digital MRV systems and data integration, including familiarity with DMRV or equivalent dMRV platforms;
  • Experience structuring, drafting and reviewing contract documentation, and providing advisory support, on carbon credit commercialisation transactions;
  • Experience managing validation, verification, and issuance cycles with accredited VVBs; and
  • Experience working with governments or development partners on energy access and carbon monetization activities in Africa

3. Technical and managerial capability of the firm (provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of key staff. Do not provide CVs of the staff. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage).

This Request for Expressions of Interest is open to all eligible firms as defined in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, as revised November 2017, August 2018, September 2023 and February 2025). Firms declared ineligible by the World Bank Group in accordance with the Bank's guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants are not eligible to participate.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) or sub-consultancy to strengthen their qualifications. In the case of a JV, firms should indicate clearly the lead firm and also whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested firms are requested to submit an Expression of Interest containing the following information:

  • Firm Profile: Organization name, legal status, country of registration, year of establishment, core business, and contact details.
  • Relevant Experience: Description of at least three (3) similar assignments completed in the last ten (10) years, including client name, project title, contract value, duration, and role of the firm. Reference contacts must be provided.
  • Approach and Methodology: A brief outline of the proposed approach to the assignment (maximum 3 pages).
  • Key Staff: Names and brief biography (maximum 2 pages each) of proposed key experts, demonstrating their qualifications and relevant experience. Do not provide full CVs of the staff.
  • Statement of Availability and Commitment: Signed declaration of the firm's availability and commitment to execute the assignment.
  • Joint Venture Agreement (if applicable): A Letter of Intent to form a JV or sub-consultancy, signed by all parties.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES

 

Country:                       Angola

Project´s Name:           Projecto de Transformação da Agropecuária Familiar (MOSAP 3)

Loan No.:                     BIRD-9396 – AO

Assignment Title:        Selection of an Individual Consultant to conduct a procurement audit covering   the 2023, 2024, and 2025 fiscal years.

Reference No.:                        179/C3/C/MOSAP3/26

The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MINAGRIF) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Smallholder Agricultural Transformation Project (MOSAP 3) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) includes (i) reviewing the procurement, contracting, and implementation processes and evaluate the quality, timeliness, reliability and appropriateness of comments and no-objections issued by the Bank for a sample of contracts, to confirm their consistency with the Legal Agreements and associated documents and ensuring that procurement, contracting and disbursement is being carried out in accordance with WB Guidelines and procedures; (ii) verifying technical compliance, physical completion and price competitiveness of each contract in the selected representative sample of contracts and expressing a professional opinion on compliance by the procurement processes with the general principle of economy and efficiency, equal opportunities, transparency; (iii) reviewing the responsibility matrix for the procurement function in the organization, delegation of procurement authority and internal control functions; the capacity of implementing agencies in handling procurement efficiently, comment on the quality of procurement and contracting, and identify reasons for delays, if any and overall, how procurement management facilitates project implementation; (iv) analyzing the risks in the various steps of procurement cycle (definition and quantification of requirements, approval of requisition, supplier sourcing, selection of procurement method, selection of contract type, bid opening and evaluation proceedings, formation of evaluation committees, approval of award, contract management, records management, use of financial securities, management of warranty/maintenance obligations, disposal of assets) and identifying any indicators of questionable standards of ethics in the procurement management and oversight environment that make the processes vulnerable to fraud and corruption or collusive and obstructive practices, and report any suspicious cases; (v) providing advice to MOSAP 3 on procurement and internal control issues and coordination with other ministries and departments on matters arising from each audit and record them in Action Plans (IPR Reports) recommending operations needed to improve project procurement performance consistent with program objectives, accuracy and completeness of the procurement records in the filling system, timely preparation of procurement information, policies and procedures that must be adopted by project management and procurement staff in ensuring orderly, economic, effective and efficient procurement operations in light of deficiencies; and all others required in the Terms of References.

The estimated level of effort is one person-month, and the contract will have a duration of 4 months, wherein it is expected that the individual consultant carries out site visit missions of about thirty (30) Calendar days. The consultant is expected to commence services no later than January 15th, 2027.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Smallholder Agriculture Transformation Project (MOSAP 3) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short listing criteria are: [a] Be proficient in procurement and contract management, [b] Have a degree in Agronomy, Business administration, Project Management, Law, Engineering; [c] Have completed at least 3 similar contracts for the past 5 years; [d] Have at least 10 years of relevant experience with World Bank’s Procurement procedures and having worked as a Senior Procurement Specialist in World Bank funded Operations for at least eight (8) years; and [e] Fluency in English and working knowledge of Portuguese language.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” [Ed. November2020 (“Procurement Regulations”)], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. The document in reference may be obtained through the following: link:https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/1783315330658711950290022020/original/ProcurementRegulations.pdf.

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants (ICS) set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, from 08:00 AM to 03:30 PM.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) by September 15th, 2026 at 15:00 (Angola time).

REPUBLIQUE DE GUINEE

Ministère deS MINES ET DE LA GEOLOGIE (MMG)

MINISTERE DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT ET DU DEVELOPPEMENT DURABLE (MEDD) PROJET DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES NATURELLES, MINIERES ET DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT (PGRNME)

 CREDIT IDA N° 6885 – GN ET DON IDA N° 8190 -GN

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR L’ÉLABORATION DES PLANS DE RESTAURATION DES SITES D’ORPAILLAGE DANS LES PREFECTURES DE SIGUIRI, MANDIANA, KOUROUSSA, DINGUIRAYE ET KANKAN EN FAVEUR DE L’AGEE

SMI N°09/PGRNME/MEDD/C/2026

       Date de fin : 16 Septembre 2026

Le Gouvernement de la République de Guinée a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir les coûts du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Minières et de l’Environnement (PGRNME), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce CREDIT IDA N° 6885 – GN et du DON IDA N° 8190 -GN pour effectuer des paiements au titre de services de consultants pour : la Recrutement d’un cabinet pour l’élaboration des plans de restauration des sites d’orpaillage dans les préfectures de Siguiri, Mandiana, Kouroussa, Dinguiraye et Kankan en faveur de l’AGEE.

Objectif de la Mission

Élaborer des Plans de restauration environnementale et sociale des sites d'orpaillage dégradés dans les préfectures de Siguiri, Mandiana, Kouroussa, Dinguiraye et Kankan, fondés sur des diagnostics techniques, environnementaux et socio-économiques, afin de restaurer durablement les écosystèmes dégradés, réduire les risques environnementaux et sociaux et fournir aux autorités compétentes des outils de planification et de mise en œuvre des actions de réhabilitation.

De façon spécifique, il s’agit de:

  • Actualiser et compléter les diagnostics environnementaux et sociaux réalisés par l'AGEE afin de caractériser l'état des sites d'orpaillage, les types de dégradations et les risques associés.
  • Identifier, analyser et hiérarchiser les impacts environnementaux, sociaux, sanitaires, sécuritaires et économiques liés aux activités d'orpaillage sur chaque site.
  • Évaluer les contraintes biophysiques, hydrologiques, géotechniques, foncières et socio-économiques susceptibles d'influencer les opérations de restauration.
  • Définir des scénarios de restauration adaptés aux caractéristiques de chaque site, en privilégiant des solutions techniques durables, économiquement viables et socialement acceptables.
  • Élaborer des plans détaillés de restauration intégrant notamment :
      • les techniques de reprofilage et de stabilisation des terrains ;
      • la restauration des sols et des cours d'eau ;
      • la revégétalisation avec des espèces locales adaptées ;
      •  les mesures de protection de la biodiversité ;
      • les mesures de gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux.
  • Proposer un programme de mise en œuvre comprenant les priorités d'intervention, le calendrier d'exécution, les coûts estimatifs, les modalités de financement et les responsabilités des différentes parties prenantes.
  • Définir un dispositif de suivi-évaluation comprenant des indicateurs de performance, des mécanismes de suivi environnemental et social ainsi que les modalités de contrôle de l'efficacité des actions de restauration.
  • Assurer la participation effective des collectivités territoriales, des services techniques déconcentrés, des communautés locales, des exploitants artisanaux et des autres parties prenantes tout au long du processus d'élaboration des plans.
  • Produire des Plans de restauration conformes aux exigences de la réglementation nationale, aux orientations de l'AGEE et aux Normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale, afin de servir de référence pour la mise en œuvre des futurs programmes de réhabilitation des sites d'orpaillage.

Les Termes de Références (TDRs) détaillés de la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Minières et de l’Environnement (PGRNME) invite les firmes de consultants (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

  • Expérience générale :
  • Avoir de l’expertise dans l’évaluations environnementales et sociales, en conception et élaboration de projets de réhabilitation et de restauration écologique et de projets socio-économiques.
  • Le Cabinet doit justifier d'au moins 10 années d'expérience dans les domaines de l'environnement, des ressources naturelles, des mines ou du développement durable.
  • Expérience spécifique :

Le cabinet devra avoir réalisé, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins dans les domaines de l'environnement, des ressources naturelles, des mines ou du développement durable

  • Trois (3) missions de réhabilitation ou de restauration de sites miniers ou de sites d'orpaillage ; ou cinq (5) missions portant sur des études environnementales et sociales (EIES, audits environnementaux, plans de fermeture de mines, plans de restauration, plans de gestion environnementale et sociale) appliquées au secteur minier.
  • Une expérience en Afrique de l'Ouest, et en particulier en Guinée, constituera un atout important.
  • Disposer d’une capacité technique et administrative en présentant les pièces requises (Agrément/RCCM, Organisation/organigramme).

Ce qui pourrait correspondre à la répartition ci-après :

  • Expérience générale (20 points) ;       
  •  Expériences spécifique (70 points) ; et
  • Capacité technique (10 points).

Le personnel clé ne sera pas évalué lors de l'établissement de la liste restreinte.

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14, 3.16, et 3.17 1.9 de la Section III de : « BANQUE MONDIALE, Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) », (Edition Septembre 2025), relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables. Veuillez noter les dispositions additionnelles suivantes relatives au conflit d’intérêts dans le cadre des Services objet de la présente Sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt :

Les Consultants ne peuvent être engagés pour des missions qui seraient incompatibles avec leurs obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients, ou qui risqueraient de les mettre dans l’impossibilité de remplir leur mandat au mieux des intérêts de l’Emprunteur. Sans préjudice du caractère général de ces dispositions, les Consultants ne peuvent être engagés dans les circonstances énoncées ci-après :

  1. Aucune entreprise engagée par l’Emprunteur pour livrer des Fournitures, réaliser des Travaux ou fournir des Services Autres que des Services des Consultants pour un projet (ni aucune entreprise affiliée qui la contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’elle contrôle elle-même ou qui est placée sous un contrôle commun) n’est admise à fournir des Services de Consultants consécutifs ou directement liés à ces Fournitures, Travaux ou Services Autres que des Services de Consultants. Cette disposition ne s’applique pas aux diverses entreprises (Consultants, entrepreneurs ou fournisseurs) qui, collectivement, s’acquittent des obligations de l’adjudicataire d’un marché clés en main ou d’un marché de conception – construction ;
  2. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION

The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) are for strengthening the management of coastal fisheries through review and gap analysis of legislative and regulatory frameworks governing coastal fisheries in the FSM states, and development of draft legislation and related recommendations, including areas relating to small boat registration and safety, community-based fisheries management, compliance, enforcement, stakeholder engagement, awareness and follow-on TORs.

The FSM Department of Resources & Development, with support from NORMA, and the State Fisheries/Marine Departments, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

1. Background and Context

FSM is an island nation in the western Pacific comprising Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae. Fisheries are a vital economic resource, and FSM’s coastal and near-shore resources are under state jurisdiction while offshore oceanic resources are retained as a national government function.

Under PROPER, FSM seeks to strengthen management of both oceanic and coastal fisheries and the critical habitats upon which they depend. The coastal component seeks to implement priority actions identified in the coastal fisheries situation analysis and related investment project profiles.

The TOR identifies that FSM lacks modern legal frameworks for coastal fisheries and that existing legislation is often not implemented or enforced. The assignment will support legislative assessment, consultation, and drafting of laws and regulations responsive to each state’s needs.

2. Assignment Objective

The objective of the assignment is to strengthen coastal fisheries management through review and gap analysis of the legal and regulatory frameworks governing coastal fisheries in the FSM states; development of draft legislation and related management recommendations; and broad stakeholder consultations across all four states, including municipalities, communities and outer island representatives where viable.

3. Scope of Services

The expected services will be delivered through the following stages:

Stage

Expected scope

Stage 1

Desk Review and Compilation of Laws and Policies

Stage 2

Legal Analysis and Gap Identification

Stage 3

Stakeholder Engagement and Site Selection - First Round

Stage 5

Stakeholder Engagement and Site Selection - Second Round

Stage 6

Stage 7

Validation Workshop

Stage 8

Stage 9

Awareness Raising and Other Activities, including TORs for subsequent consultancies

Stage 10

Final Consultancy Report

The assignment is expected to require field work and consultations in all four FSM states, as well as desk-based legal and policy analysis, legislative drafting, reporting and support to stakeholder validation.

4. Expected Duration and Indicative Level of Effort

The total duration of the assignment is expected to be fourteen (14) months. The TOR indicates an expected total input of approximately twenty-five (25) person-months by key experts, working part-time across the assignment. The final team composition, level of effort and work plan will be proposed by the selected Consultant in its technical and financial proposals and confirmed during negotiations.

6. Required Consultant Profile and Experience

Interested consulting firms should demonstrate relevant experience and qualifications in the following areas:

  • Legal and regulatory review, gap analysis and legislative drafting for fisheries, marine resources, maritime safety, natural resources, environment or related sectors.
  • Coastal fisheries management, community-based fisheries management, compliance and enforcement, and sustainable fisheries policy, preferably in Pacific Island countries or small island developing states.
  • Experience supporting national and subnational/state government agencies with legal reform, stakeholder consultation and validation workshops.
  • Experience with small boat registration, vessel safety, minimum safety standards, licensing, compliance systems or related maritime/fisheries regulatory reforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage participatory consultation processes involving government, communities, municipalities, NGOs, outer island representatives and other stakeholders.
  • Experience preparing clear, practical reports, legislative drafting instructions, draft legal instruments, management recommendations, training/awareness TORs and final consolidated reports.
  • Demonstrated institutional capacity, project management systems and quality assurance procedures to deliver a 14-month multi-state assignment.

The indicative key expertise identified in the TOR includes Fisheries Legal Expert; Fisheries Management Specialist / Fisheries Policy and Development Planner; National Local Liaison / Community Facilitator; and National Legal Expert. Key experts and CVs should not be evaluated at the EOI shortlisting stage unless expressly required by the Bank-approved procurement documents; detailed staffing will be evaluated at the proposal stage.

7. Shortlisting Criteria

The Borrower will assess Expressions of Interest to determine the shortlist of qualified firms. The criteria below are proposed for use in the shortlisting assessment. The EOI evaluation should focus on the firm’s qualifications and experience, not on individual experts or detailed methodology.

Criterion

Indicative assessment considerations

Core business and years in business

Relevance of the firm’s core business to legal reform, fisheries/marine governance, natural resources, maritime safety, stakeholder consultation and policy/regulatory support; demonstrated operational history.

Relevant assignment experience

Similar assignments completed in legislative review, legal gap analysis, fisheries/coastal resource legal frameworks, community-based fisheries management, enforcement/compliance, maritime/small boat safety, and subnational legal drafting.

Technical and managerial capability

Firm’s capacity to manage a multi-disciplinary assignment across four FSM states over 14 months, including quality assurance, consultation logistics, reporting, legislative drafting, and coordination with government agencies.

Pacific / FSM / small island context experience

Experience working in Pacific Island countries, FSM, small island developing states, customary/community settings, outer island communities, and multi-jurisdictional state/national governance environments.

Team/partnership strength

Strength and relevance of team, JV, sub-consultant arrangements proposed to cover national legal systems, local liaison, community consultation and specialized technical expertise.

8. Selection Method and Next Step

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers 7th Edition, September 2025. Under CQS, firms provide information on relevant experience and qualifications; the Borrower selects the firm with the best qualifications and relevant experience and invites that firm to submit technical and financial proposals for negotiations.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers 7th edition, September 2025, including provisions on conflict of interest, eligibility, fraud and corruption, and the Bank’s sanctions framework. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF NIGERIA

FEDERAL MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND SANITATION

IN COLLABORATION WITH THE FEDERAL MINISTRY OF POWER

SUSTAINABLE POWER AND IRRIGATION FOR NIGERIA (SPIN) PROJECT

IDA Credit No: IDA-76370

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES

Assignment Title: ENGAGEMENT OF A CONSULTING FIRM FOR HYDROPOWER PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS (PPP) PROCESS AND GUIDELINES REVIEW

Reference No.: FMWR&S/SPIN/QCBS/CS/2026/013

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN), through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (FMWRS) in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Power (FMP), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to finance the engagement of a Consulting Firm for the Hydropower Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) Process and Guidelines Review.

The SPIN Project is designed to strengthen dam safety and improve the management of water resources for hydropower and irrigation in selected areas of Nigeria. The FGN through the development of a Hydropower Master Plan (HMP) seeks to increase collaboration between the FMWR&S and the FMP to attract private investment and partnerships in the hydropower sector. This requires an assessment of the existing legal, regulatory, institutional, and procedural frameworks governing private sector participation in the development and operation of brownfield and greenfield hydropower projects, to support efficient, transparent, and bankable implementation of the HMP.

Purpose of the Assignment

The consulting services ("the Services") seek to engage a qualified and competent consulting firm ("the PPP Advisory Firm") to assess the applicability and effectiveness of Nigeria's existing PPP legal, regulatory, and institutional frameworks as they apply to hydropower project development, and to provide recommendations for their enhancement, subject to the approval of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC). The assignment will further support institutional capacity building for relevant stakeholders to strengthen readiness for effective implementation of the Hydropower Master Plan.

The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Power, through the Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU) of the SPIN Project, now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. WEST AFRICAN POWER POOL

Project:  WAPP GHANA-CÔTE D’IVOIRE INTERCONNECTION REINFORCEMENT PROJECT

NOTICE OF INTERNATIONAL RECRUITMENT

Revised 23.8.2026

Consultant Services

Selection of individual consultant

Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

Financing: World Bank IDA

Don IDA No: E4040

Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV

Open to: All eligible individuals

Duty Station: Abomey-Calavi, Benin

Application Deadline: 24 September 2024

 

  1. CONTEXT

The West African Power Pool (WAPP) was created by the highest decision-making authority of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) at the Conference of Heads of State and Government of the Member States held in Lomé, in December 1999. The Headquarters of the WAPP Secretariat is in Abomey-Calavi, Republic of Benin.

The ECOWAS strategic objective being implemented by the West African Power Pool (WAPP) is based on a dynamic vision of integrating national power grids into a unified regional electricity market, so that such a mechanism would, over the medium and long term, ensure to the ECOWAS citizens access to adequate power quality at an affordable price, and enhance the economic development of the Member States including industrialization growth, Health and Education improvement, Poverty Reduction, various Employment Opportunities Creation, etc…

To achieve its vision of operationalizing a unified ECOWAS regional electricity market, the WAPP Information and Coordination Centre (WAPP ICC), a Department within the WAPP Secretariat has been designated to perform the functions of a System Market Operator (SMO) responsible for coordinating the reliability of the WAPP Interconnected Transmission System (WAPPITS) made up of the power systems of fourteen (14) ECOWAS Member Countries and administration of the regional electricity market.

To this end, the WAPP Secretariat with the support of the World Bank within the Project “WAPP Côte d’Ivoire Interconnection and operationalization of the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market” intends to reinforce staffing of the ICC Department by filling a key vacant position, that of a Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

The Engineer will be selected competitively, and the successful candidates will be joining the current team in the Information and Coordination Centre (ICC) as it prepares to operationalize the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market.

2. ROLE OVERVIEW

Under the supervision of the Head of the System Operations Coordination Division, the Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer is responsible for the management of the ICC's Power System Database. He/She extracts data from various sources (APIs, HIVE tables, and other structured and unstructured data sources) to process and store large volumes of data, ensuring their accuracy, consistency and security. He/She develops reporting dashboards and analytical tools to support the analysis of power system operations, and supports the design, testing and implementation of models and databases for all systems requiring the WAPP Network Model.

The detailed Job description for the assignment may be consulted and/or downloaded from the WAPP website at: www.ecowapp.org/en/tenders

The WAPP General Secretariat invites eligible Individual Consultants to express their interest in providing the required Services described in the Job decription. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services by submitting: (a) a cover letter/motivation letter, and (b) an up-to-date detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV).

WAPP is an equal opportunity employer that offers equal chances to men and women. Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply.  

3. LANGUAGE

Good oral and written communication skills in English and French  

4. DURATION OF MISSION

The successful candidate shall be offered an initial Consultancy Contract of approximatively 17 months from the beginning of the assignment ( i.e.until April 30, 2028). Upon completion of the World Bank funding, the position shall be absorbed by WAPP.

The beginning of the assignment is planned for November 2026

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the method of "Selection of Individual Consultants" described in the World Bank "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (edition September 2025).  

6. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Applications must be submitted exclusively by email and should bear the subject line: “Application for ICC Engineer- Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV”.

Paper applications will not be accepted.

Applications may be submitted in either French or English and should be sent to: procurement@ecowapp.org

 Particular emphasis should be placed on references for relevant similar assignments previously carried out, which should be clearly highlighted and described.

Deadline for submission of applications:  September 24, 2026, at noon, 12:00 pm, Benin local time (GMT+1).

Further information may be obtained by sending an email to:

spos@ecowapp.org

With copies to:

cpm@ecowapp.org

 hdhra@ecowapp.org

Only shortlisted candidates shall be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

 

Country:  MOZAMBIQUE

Project:  Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project

Agreement: Preparation Advance No. -V522-MZ.

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.

 

Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.
